item.title: Try new camping gear in your trunk before you buy – SugarMount
item.description:
Before you buy gear · Android app

Fit it in the trunk before you buy it

Will this tent still fit with everything else? Before you check out, put the new gear into your trunk next to what you already pack, and see whether it all fits.

Get TrimBox on Google PlayAbout TrimBox
  • 197 camping items
  • Enter any size yourself
  • Leftovers listed by name

  • Your usual load, plus one

    Add the gear you always take, or open a saved layout, then add the item you are thinking of buying. If it isn't listed, enter its size.

  • How many fit, and what's left

    It says "15 of 16 items fit" and lists what is left by name, plus how many a repack would fit.

  • Tall gear and the tailgate

    Tall coolers and boxes tend to hit the sloped tailgate. If one does, it turns red and shows how far it sticks out.

Check before you buy

  1. Load what you already take: add your usual camping gear, or open a saved layout from My layouts.
  2. Add the new item: find it among 197 camping items, or use Custom and enter the packed size from the product page (folded, not set up).
  3. Tap Will it fit?: see whether everything fits, or what is left over and why. Try Repack, and on the Sorento, IONIQ 5, Carnival 7-seat, Ray, Casper or Casper Electric it can suggest sliding the 2nd row a few centimeters.

You can also try the same gear in another car. Switch vehicles and your gear stays, so you can compare your current car and your next one with the same load.

Good to know

  • Every item is treated as a box of its width, depth and height, so round bags and folding chairs may take a little more room than in real life.
  • Sleeping bags and soft bags are squeezed only as much as needed. Listed coolers and heaters that must stay upright are kept upright.
  • Weights are estimates from product data or typical values for the item type.
  • The Sorento is checked against published tape measurements; the other nine vehicles are estimated from specs and may be off by a few centimeters.

Frequently asked questions

The item I want isn't listed.

Open Custom in the gear picker and enter a name, width, depth and height. Use the packed size from the product page, the size in its carry bag.

Do I have to add my usual gear every time?

No. Your current layout saves automatically, and you can save named layouts. Named saves start with 1 slot and gain one more for each short ad you watch, up to 5. Pro (one-time purchase) has no slot limit.

I'm also thinking about a new car.

Switch the vehicle and repack; your gear stays. Apart from the Sorento, the trunk shapes are estimated from specs, so check a real trunk before you decide on a car.

Does it need internet?

The check, auto-pack and saving work without internet. Only ads, usage analytics and the Pro purchase use it.

Trunk first, then checkout.

Try your usual gear and the new item in your car together.

Get TrimBox on Google Play

  • Pack the car on your phone before a camping trip
  • Will your winter camping gear fit too?
  • Check the trunk before you buy a roof box
  • Trunk sizes of 10 mini cars, SUVs and minivans

item.title: Pack the car on your phone before a camping trip – SugarMount
item.description:
Camping gear, packed first · Android app

Pack the car on your phone before you pack the car

Will all of this fit in the trunk? Find out at home, not in the parking lot. TrimBox packs your camping gear into the shape of your trunk and tells you whether the tailgate will close.

Get TrimBox on Google PlayAbout TrimBox
  • 10 mini cars, SUVs and minivans
  • 197 camping items
  • Sorento checked against published tape measurements

  • See if the tailgate closes

    If the top of the load hits the sloped tailgate, it turns red and shows how many centimeters stick out.

  • See what's left over

    Items that don't fit are listed by name, with how many a repack would fit and whether sliding the 2nd row would do it.

  • Know what to load first

    Every item gets a number. Heavy things go low, and the cooler you reach for often ends up near the tailgate.

How it works

  1. Pick your car: Kia Sorento, Hyundai Santa Fe, Hyundai Palisade, Kia Carnival, Kia Sportage, Tesla Model Y, Hyundai IONIQ 5, Kia Ray, Hyundai Casper or Hyundai Casper Electric. For any other car, enter the trunk width, depth and height to get a box shape.
  2. Add your gear: choose from 197 camping items (tents, tarps, tables, chairs, coolers, sleeping bags) or add a whole set: Minimal for 2, Family of 4 or Solo backpacking. Each item goes into the trunk as you add it.
  3. Tap Will it fit?: see whether the layout fits as it is, and if not, which items are blocked and why.
  4. Load in order: step through the loading guide one item at a time. The layout saves itself, so it is there again when you pack up to go home.

Show it instead of explaining it

Turn the layout and the numbered loading order into one card and send it to whoever is helping you pack.

Sizes can differ from your car. The Sorento is checked against published tape measurements, though some values such as height and tailgate slope are estimates. The other nine vehicles are estimated from specs and official cargo volumes, so they may be off by a few centimeters. Leave some room for tight fits. Under-floor storage and the Model Y and IONIQ 5 front trunks are not counted yet.

Frequently asked questions

Does it need internet?

The check, auto-pack and saving work without internet. Only ads, usage analytics and the Pro purchase use it, so you can open a saved layout at a campsite with a weak signal.

Does it cost anything?

It is free to install and shows ads. Nothing is shown while you pick gear, pack, check or follow the loading steps. Pro, a one-time purchase rather than a subscription, removes the ads and makes named saves unlimited.

My car isn't on the list.

Enter the trunk width, depth and height (wheel arches optional) to see it as a box. Tap Request a vehicle at the bottom of the vehicle menu; we add vehicles in order of requests.

Are my layouts sent anywhere?

No. Layouts and their names stay on your phone, and we run no servers. Cards and layout files leave only when you share them. See the TrimBox privacy policy.

Fit it first. Then go.

Pack this trip's gear into your car before you leave.

  • Will your winter camping gear fit too?
  • Check the trunk before you buy a roof box

item.title: Before a roof box, check what fits in the trunk – SugarMount
item.description:
Thinking about a roof box · Android app

Check the trunk before you buy a roof box

Whether you need a roof box depends on how much of your gear fits in the trunk. Pack your camping gear into the trunk on your phone first, and see what is left over.

Get TrimBox on Google PlayAbout TrimBox
  • Shape, not just liters
  • Leftovers listed by name
  • 10 mini cars, SUVs and minivans

  • Leftovers, right away

    If the trunk can't take everything, the items that don't fit are listed by name. Those are the ones that need the roof or somewhere else.

  • Shape, not just liters

    Two trunks with the same liters can take different loads because of wheel arches, a sloped tailgate and a dropping ceiling. Each vehicle has its own shape.

  • Stack high, and still close

    Stacking up to fill the trunk is where loads hit the sloped tailgate. Anything that does turns red, with how far it sticks out.

A roof box decision, in this order

  1. Add the whole trip's gear: tents, tarps, tables, chairs, coolers and sleeping bags from the list, or a ready-made set.
  2. Tap Will it fit?: if everything fits, the trunk is enough. If not, see what is left over.
  3. Try Repack and the 2nd-row tip: see whether a new layout or sliding the 2nd row a little solves it (Sorento, IONIQ 5, Carnival 7-seat).
  4. Still left over?: use the size and number of the leftovers to judge how much extra space you need.

TrimBox only counts the inside of the trunk. It does not model roof boxes, roof bags or trunk organizers themselves. The Sorento is checked against published tape measurements; the other nine vehicles are estimated from specs and may be off by a few centimeters.

Frequently asked questions

Does it tell me what size roof box to buy?

No. Roof boxes are not modeled. It shows which items don't fit in the trunk and how big they are, so you can choose a roof box from that.

What about trunk organizers or folding crates?

Folding crates and storage boxes are on the list, and any other organizer can be added as a box by its width, depth and height. Small things that go inside it don't need to be added.

Does sliding the 2nd row really help?

On the Sorento, IONIQ 5, Carnival 7-seat, Ray, Casper and Casper Electric you can choose a forward 2nd-row position and check again, and the result sheet may suggest how many centimeters would fit everything. Check that the rear seats still have room in the real car.

Does it cost anything?

It is free to install and shows ads. Nothing is shown while you pick gear, pack, check or follow the loading steps.

Trunk first, then the roof.

See how much of this trip's gear the trunk can take.

Get TrimBox on Google Play

  • Trunk sizes of 10 mini cars, SUVs and minivans
  • Try new camping gear in your trunk before you buy
  • Pack the car on your phone before a camping trip

item.title: Trunk sizes of 10 SUVs, minivans and mini cars – SugarMount
item.description:
Trunk size by vehicle · November 2026

How much camping gear fits in your trunk?

Liters alone don't tell you whether the tent and cooler fit. Here are the floor sizes and heights of 10 trunks, from SUVs and minivans to mini cars, and how much of a camping load fits in each.

Get TrimBox on Google PlayAbout TrimBox
  • Sorento checked against published tape measurements
  • Other nine estimated from specs

At a glance

These are the trunk values TrimBox 1.0.2 uses, in centimeters. Floor is the width between the wheel arches × the depth from the 2nd-row seatback to the opening. Height is floor to ceiling → top of the opening.

Vehicle (setup)FloorMax widthHeight → openingApp volumeFamily setShape
Sorento 5- and 7-seat109 × 10713882 → 79≈ 951 L16/16Measured
Santa Fe 5- and 7-seat108 × 10413687 → 82≈ 970 L16/16Estimated
Palisade 7-seat115 × 12213584 → 80≈ 1,142 L16/16Estimated
Carnival 3rd row up127 × 68127150 → 145≈ 895 L15/16Estimated
Carnival 7-seat, 3rd row stowed127 × 145150112 → 105≈ 2,006 L16/16Estimated
Carnival 9-seat, 3rd row tipped up and slid fully forward, 4th stowed127 × 110150112 → 105≈ 1,589 L16/16Estimated
Sportage104 × 9413680 → 73≈ 707 L14/16Estimated
Model Y94 × 11010480 → 80≈ 623 L12/16Estimated
IONIQ 5105 × 10011480 → 71≈ 660 L12/16Estimated
Ray, 2nd row up93 × 33–53118118 → 113≈ 236–497 L–Estimated
Ray, 2nd row folded93 × 13011898 → 93≈ 1,272 L–Estimated
Casper, 2nd row up96 × 37–5312095 → 92≈ 255–428 L–Estimated
Casper, 2nd row folded96 × 97–11312078 → 72≈ 816–959 L–Estimated
Casper Electric, 2nd row up96 × 47–6312077 → 74≈ 291–435 L–Estimated
Casper Electric, 2nd row folded96 × 108–12412077 → 72≈ 906–1,047 L–Estimated

7-seat SUVs with the 3rd row folded, 2nd row in its rearmost position. Mini cars show the range from the 2nd row all the way back to all the way forward, and are checked with a solo car camping load instead of the family set (see the mini car section). Family set is the app's Family of 4 set (a 4-person tunnel tent, a large tarp, a roll table, 4 folding chairs, a 50 L cooler, 4 three-season sleeping bags, a two-burner stove, a cook set, a storage box and a bundle of firewood), packed with TrimBox 1.0.0 auto-pack on November 8, 2026 (items packed / 16).

Why app volume differs from the brochure

Brochure trunk volumes (VDA) are usually measured with 1-liter blocks up to the cover or window line, which is not how camping gear is packed. The app volume is the space from the floor behind the 2nd row up to the ceiling, where the tailgate still closes, in the app's trunk shape. It comes out larger than the brochure figure, and two trunks with the same liters can still take different loads because of wheel arches, a sloped tailgate and a dropping ceiling.

Kia Sorento trunk size (MQ4)

The Sorento MQ4 (2021+ model year in the US) 5-seat and 7-seat with the 3rd row folded share the same space above the floor. The floor is 109 cm between the wheel arches and 107 cm deep, widening to 138 cm only in the last 38 cm by the tailgate. Height is 82 cm, 79 cm at the opening. You can also choose the 2nd row slid 13 cm or 27 cm forward.

Width and depth are checked against published tape measurements; height, wheel-arch length and tailgate slope are estimates. The app volume of about 951 L is a little below ADAC's 980 to 1,000 L measured to the ceiling behind the 2nd row. All 16 items of the family set fit with the 2nd row all the way back.

Hyundai Santa Fe trunk size (MX5)

The Santa Fe MX5 (2024+ model year) 5-seat and 7-seat with the 3rd row folded share the same space above the floor and differ only in under-floor storage. The floor is 108 × 104 cm and the height 87 cm, 82 cm at the opening: a little shorter and taller than the Sorento. The opening is about 127 cm wide at the floor.

The app volume of about 970 L is matched to ADAC's 975 L measured to the ceiling behind the 2nd row. There is no 2nd-row slide option. All 16 family items fit.

Hyundai Palisade trunk size (LX3)

The Palisade LX3 (2026+ model year) is included as a 7-seat with the 3rd row folded. Its 115 × 122 cm floor is the longest of the supported SUVs. Height is 84 cm, 80 cm at the opening.

With no official interior dimensions, the shape is matched to about 1,140 L: the US 3rd-row-folded volume (SAE 1,311 L) scaled by the same ratio as the Sorento. All 16 family items fit.

Kia Carnival trunk size (KA4)

The Carnival KA4 has three setups. 3rd row up means loading into the well behind the rear bench (floor 127 × 68 cm). The opening's sill is about 40 cm above the well floor, and you can stack up to 150 cm. The well is short, so 15 of the 16 family items fit.

7-seat, 3rd row stowed gives a flat floor of 127 × 145 cm (about 2,006 L), with the 2nd row slid 6 cm or 12 cm forward as options. 9-seat, 3rd row tipped up, 4th stowed assumes the 4th row is in the well and the 3rd-row seats are tipped up and slid all the way forward, so nobody can sit in the 3rd row. The folded 3rd row is the front wall, so the floor is 110 cm deep (about 1,589 L; no official figure to compare). All 16 family items fit in both. With no official interior dimensions, these shapes are worked back from official volumes (VDA and SAE).

Kia Sportage trunk size (NQ5)

This is the long-wheelbase Sportage NQ5 sold in Korea and North America. The floor is 104 × 94 cm and the height 80 cm, 73 cm at the opening. Published tape measurements exist only for the shorter European body, so the length is estimated from that. The app volume is about 707 L.

14 of the 16 family items fit. If you pack a lot, check in the app what is left over.

Tesla Model Y trunk size (2025+)

The Model Y (2025+) is 94 cm between the wheel arches, 110 cm deep and 80 cm high. The back slopes down, so the higher you stack, the narrower it gets toward the tailgate.

The app volume of about 623 L is above ADAC's block-measured 540 L to the ceiling (blocks fill less of the space under the sloped glass). The deep under-floor well (about 105 L by ADAC) and the front trunk are not counted yet. 12 of the 16 family items fit. With the under-floor well you may fit more in the real car.

Hyundai IONIQ 5 trunk size (2024+)

The IONIQ 5 facelift (2024+) has a 105 × 100 cm floor with the 2nd row all the way back, a height of 80 cm, 71 cm at the opening, and a 3 cm sill. You can also choose the 2nd row slid 7 cm or 14 cm forward.

The app volume of about 660 L is about 10% above ADAC's 600 L to the ceiling behind the 2nd row. With the 2nd row back, 12 of the 16 family items fit; with the 2nd row all the way forward (about 14 cm), 15 fit. The front trunk and the under-floor box (about 40 L by ADAC) are not counted.

Kia Ray and Hyundai Casper trunk size (mini cars)

The mini cars are there for solo car camping. The Kia Ray (facelift from September 2022; the Ray EV has the same trunk) has a 93 × 33 cm floor with the 2nd row up and all the way back, and you can also choose the 2nd row slid 10 cm or 20 cm forward. It is tall instead: 118 cm, 113 cm at the opening. With the 2nd row folded the floor is 93 × 130 cm, 98 cm high and 93 cm at the opening.

The Hyundai Casper (from September 2021, including the October 2024 refresh) has a 96 × 37 cm trunk well with the 2nd row up, 95 cm high and 92 cm at the opening, with a sill 25 cm above the floor. With the 2nd row folded it is 96 × 97 cm, 78 cm high and 72 cm at the opening. The Casper Electric (from August 2024) has a 96 × 47 cm floor, 96 × 108 cm with the 2nd row folded, and 77 cm of height. Both can also take the 2nd row slid 8 cm or 16 cm forward. When you first pick a mini car, it starts with the 2nd row all the way forward.

The app volume is matched to the official figures: about 1,272 L for the Ray with the 2nd row folded (official 1,324 L) and about 291 L for the Casper Electric with the 2nd row up (official 280 L; the Casper's official 166–301 L is measured only up to the cargo cover). With the 2nd row up and all the way back, the 10 solo car camping items (a car camping mat, a self-inflating mat, a sleeping bag, a small cooler, a folding box, a single burner, a chair, a two-person table, car window curtains and a 12 V heated pad) don't all fit in the Ray or the Casper. With the 2nd row folded, all 10 fit in the Ray, the Casper and the Casper Electric, and the Ray and the Casper Electric take all 16 family items too. A folded 2nd row counts as cargo space only; TrimBox does not judge whether there is room to lie down. Under-floor storage is not counted.

  • Same gear, another car

    Switch vehicles and your gear stays. Tap Repack to load it into the other trunk.

  • Leftovers, by name

    Items that don't fit are listed by name, and cars with a sliding 2nd row get a tip on how far to slide it.

  • Tailgate check

    Each vehicle's tailgate slope is different. If the load hits it, it turns red.

Frequently asked questions

Are these official dimensions?

No. Carmakers rarely publish trunk length and width. The Sorento values are checked against published tape measurements; the others are estimated from official volumes, body specs and published measurements, and may differ from your car by a few centimeters.

My own measurements are different.

Send your tape measurements to sugarmount21@gmail.com and we will consider them for the next version. Please say what you measured from where (floor width, between the wheel arches, depth, opening height).

My car isn't on the list.

Only these 10 vehicles (17 setups) for now. Any other car can be entered as a box by its trunk width, depth and height. Tap Request a vehicle in the vehicle menu; we add vehicles in order of requests.

Does it support SUVs with the 3rd row up?

SUVs are 5-seat or 7-seat with the 3rd row folded. Only the Carnival is included with the 3rd row up.

Measure with your gear, not just liters.

Pick this trip's gear and load it into your own trunk.

Get TrimBox on Google Play

More camping packing guides

  • Pack the car on your phone before a camping trip
  • Check the trunk before you buy a roof box
  • Will your winter camping gear fit too?

TrimBox is an independent app, not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Kia, Hyundai or Tesla. Kia, Sorento, Carnival, Sportage, Hyundai, Santa Fe, Palisade, IONIQ, Tesla and Model Y are trademarks of their respective owners, used only to identify supported vehicles. item.title: Will your winter camping gear fit the trunk? – SugarMount
item.description:
Winter camping gear · Android app

Will your winter gear fit too?

Add a heater, a heated blanket and thicker sleeping bags, and the usual load stops fitting. The night before, pack your winter camping gear into the trunk on your phone first.

Get TrimBox on Google PlayAbout TrimBox
  • Heaters and fuel cans stay upright
  • Leftovers listed by name
  • Tailgate check

  • Heaters and fuel cans are on the list

    Kerosene fan heater (large, 9 L), Kerosene heater (large, round, 7 L), Kerosene heater (large, square), a small camping kerosene heater, Kerosene can (20 L, full) and Kerosene can (10 L, full) are listed, along with a 12V heated blanket, 3-season, down and double sleeping bags and air mats.

  • See what's left over

    When the load grows past the trunk, the leftovers are listed by name, so you can decide at home what stays behind.

  • Load in order on a cold morning

    Every item gets a number. Follow the guide and you won't be unloading and reloading in a freezing parking lot.

Why winter loads overflow

Winter gear is bulkier for the same number of people. A heater has to stand upright, and winter sleeping bags and thick mats take more room. Two trunks with the same liters can take different loads because of the wheel arches, the sloped tailgate and a ceiling that drops toward the back.

TrimBox packs into each vehicle's own trunk shape. Items that must stay upright, like heaters, fuel cans and coolers, are kept upright, items of 20 kg or more stay on the floor, and soft items like sleeping bags are squeezed only as much as needed.

How to check a winter load

  1. Open your usual load: open a layout saved from your last trip, or start from a set such as Family of 4.
  2. Add the winter gear: add a heater, a fuel can, the heated blanket and sleeping bags from the list. Use Custom only for anything that is not listed.
  3. Tap Will it fit?: see whether it all fits, what is left over and whether the tailgate closes. Save the layout and it is ready again when you pack up.

Sizes can differ from your car. The Sorento is checked against published tape measurements; the other nine vehicles are estimated from specs and official cargo volumes. Under-floor storage is not counted. TrimBox does not judge how to carry fuel or a heater in a car; follow the maker's instructions.

Frequently asked questions

Which heaters and fuel cans are listed?

A large 9 L kerosene fan heater, kerosene heaters (large round 7 L, large square 7.5 L and a small camping one) and kerosene cans (20 L and 10 L, weighed full). If yours is a very different size, enter its outside size including the handle in Custom.

Will it lay the heater on its side?

Listed heaters, fuel cans and coolers are always kept upright. Items you enter yourself may be laid down to fit, so check the result if yours must stand.

Can I use it when packing up at the campsite?

Yes. Layouts stay on your phone, and the check, auto-pack and saving work without internet. Only ads, usage analytics and the Pro purchase use it.

Which cars does it support?

Kia Sorento, Hyundai Santa Fe, Hyundai Palisade, Kia Carnival, Kia Sportage, Tesla Model Y, Hyundai IONIQ 5, Kia Ray, Hyundai Casper and Hyundai Casper Electric. Any other car can be entered as a box. See trunk sizes by vehicle.

Pack it in the warm living room, not the cold parking lot.

Fit your winter camping gear before you leave.

Get TrimBox on Google Play

  • Try new camping gear in your trunk before you buy
  • Check the trunk before you buy a roof box

item.title: Share a family calendar and decide who does what – SugarMount
item.description:
Help · Android

Share a family calendar and decide who does what

Putting every event in one place is only half of it. When each to-do also shows who is on it, nobody has to ask twice. Here is how to set that up with AXFamily, a shared family calendar for Android.

This guide is based on AXFamily 1.2.0, an Android app by SugarMount. Every name and event in the text and screens is made up.

What goes wrong when plans live in a group chat

A family group chat is quick, but it is a poor place to keep a schedule. New messages push last week's class timetable out of sight, and "who said they'd do that?" comes up again.

  • Nobody's name stays on the task. "I'll handle it" gets buried in the thread and never reaches a calendar.
  • Clashes are easy to miss. When a child's swim class and an adult's meeting sit in two different calendars, no one notices they overlap.
  • Shared and private plans get mixed. You can't post a surprise gift run in the family chat.

So a family calendar that lasts settles three things: where plans go, who can see them, and who takes care of them. The steps below go through them in that order.

Step 1: Create your family and invite people

  1. Create a family — Sign up with a Google account or email the first time you open the app, and give your family a name. Accounts are for adults 19 or older.
  2. Invite adults — On the Family tab, tap Invite family → Send invite message. The app writes a message with an invite code, and your phone's share sheet sends it to your partner or the kids' grandparents.
  3. Accept the invite — The other person installs the app, taps I was invited and pastes the message. Each code works once and expires, so send it only to the person you are inviting.
  4. Add kids as profiles — Kids don't sign up. Add them as a profile with a name and birthday; they don't need a phone. Birthday reminders are set here too.

The person who created the family (the owner) or an admin can invite. The simplest start: one adult creates the family, then invites the other adults who look after the kids, one at a time.

Step 2: Choose who sees what

AXFamily is a shared calendar, but new events and records start private. You widen only the plans your family needs to see. Open an event and tap its sharing setting to get the Who can see sheet.

SettingWho sees itGood for
Only meOnly you. Not even the family admin.Buying a surprise gift, your own doctor's appointment
Selected peopleThe family members you pick.A meeting with a child's tutor that two adults need to know about
Whole familyEveryone in the family now and anyone who joins later.School runs, family events, trips

With Time only, your family sees that you are busy at that time, but not the title or details. It works well for work meetings you don't want to share but still need to block out.

Items you keep private never show up when someone else asks the AI assistant. A family admin can't open another adult's private items either.

Step 3: Decide who does what with "I'll do it"

Once plans are in one place, decide who handles each one. In AXFamily every to-do keeps the name of the person who took it.

  1. Add a task — Tap Add task and enter a title and a due date. For a list of things to bring, add them as a Checklist (up to 50 items).
  2. Ask someone — To hand it to another family member, ask them to do it. A card such as "Dogyeom Yoon asked you to take this" appears on their Today tab.
  3. "I'll do it" or "Can't do it" — When they tap I'll do it, the family sees they are on it. If they can't this time, they tap Can't do it, and you see the reply so you can ask someone else.
  4. Check things off — Tick checklist items as they are done (after the task is taken). With notifications on, you get a reminder before the due date.

You don't have to ask first. On a task the whole family can see, anyone can tap I'll do it on something nobody has taken yet.

Sharing school runs and class pick-ups with grandparents

If grandparents help with drop-offs and pick-ups, the key is deciding which adult goes along to each child's event. A made-up week might look like this:

Child's eventRepeatGoes along
Seoa's swim class (Wed 4:30 PM)Every weekGrandma
Jiho art class (Tue, Thu 3:00 PM)Every weekDogyeom
Seoa piano (Fri 5:00 PM)Every weekNot decided yet
  1. Make kids' classes repeat — When you add the event, set Repeat to every week and choose an end date or a number of times. Add only the child under With.
  2. Pick who goes along — If an event with only a child on it has no adult going along, the Sunday heads-up and the Today tab show it as "No one to go along". Tap I'll do it on that line and a to-do such as "Go with: Seoa piano" is created in your name.
  3. See clashes early — If a child's event overlaps another event of the adult going along, it shows up under Overlapping plans, like Seoa's swim class and a team meeting in the screen below.

If grandparents find a new app hard, start by just looking at the Sunday heads-up together. They only need to tap the things they can take.

Check the week together on Sunday evening

A shared calendar lasts when the family looks at it together once a week. With notifications on, AXFamily gathers the coming week every Sunday evening:

  • No one assigned — to-dos nobody took, and children's events with no adult going along
  • Overlapping plans — a child's event that clashes with the companion's other plans
  • Due — to-dos due this week and who has them
  • Birthdays — family birthdays within 7 days

It arrives at 8 PM by default, and you can change the time in settings. The list is made on your phone, and the notification shows counts only, never titles or names. The Sunday heads-up is free and doesn't count toward AI uses.

Small rules that keep a family calendar going

  • One person per to-do. "Either of us" often ends up as neither. Even for shared jobs, one person keeps track.
  • Family plans for the family, yours for you. Don't share everything on day one; widen only what others need. Work meetings can be "Time only".
  • Weekly things repeat. Classes and practice that happen every week go in once as a repeating event.
  • Five minutes on Sunday. When the heads-up arrives, sort out the unassigned items first and talk about any clash that day.

What it can't do

  • It's an Android app. It runs on Android 12L or later and needs the internet, since your family shares records.
  • It doesn't sync with other calendar apps. Add events from another calendar yourself, or take a screenshot and use Add to organize it.
  • Notifications must be allowed on the phone. If the app's notifications are off in phone settings, event reminders and the Sunday heads-up won't arrive.
  • None of this needs AI. Invites, sharing settings, "I'll do it", repeating events and the Sunday heads-up all work without AI.

FAQ

Is the shared family calendar free?

Events, to-dos, reminders, the Sunday heads-up and sharing settings are free, with one banner ad at the bottom of the screen. The Family Plus subscription removes ads for the whole family and adds more AI uses.

Can my partner see all my events?

No. New events start private. Only events you switch to the whole family or to selected people are visible. Not even the family admin can see your private events.

Do kids need an account?

No. Kids are added as profiles without signing up, and they don't need a phone.

What happens when grandma taps "Can't do it"?

The task shows "{name} replied they can't do it" to the person who asked. They can tap New task with same details to ask someone else, or take care of it themselves.

Can the weekly heads-up come on another day?

The day is fixed to Sunday; only the time can change. During the week, the Today tab's Needs attention shows to-dos due soon with no one assigned, overlapping plans and children's events with no one going along.

Related articles

  • School notices and class schedules in one calendar
  • Plan a trip around naps, then keep photos together

About AXFamily

A shared family calendar for Android that gathers your family's events and to-dos in one place and shows who's on each one. New items are private by default.

Get AXFamily on Google PlayAbout the AXFamily app

See the AXFamily privacy policy and the AXFamily terms of service.

item.title: Plan a trip around naps, then keep photos together – SugarMount
item.description:
Help · Android

Plan a trip around naps, then keep photos together

With kids, the hard part of a trip is the timetable more than the place. Here is one flow for a plan that fits naps and meals, a packing list that remembers what you forgot, and photos sorted afterwards.

This guide is based on AXFamily 1.2.0, an Android app by SugarMount. Every family, place and event in the text and screens is made up. The trip planner and family memories are AI features, so each adult who wants them turns on AI with their own consent.

Start with your family's daily rhythm

Naps and meals are the first things a trip schedule breaks. In AXFamily, write down each person's daily rhythm, and trip and weekend plans put rest and meal times around it.

  • Where — On the Family tab, open a person to find their daily rhythm: wake up, nap, lunch, dinner and bedtime. Anything left empty uses a general guide.
  • Who sees it — Daily rhythms are visible to the whole family.
  • Kids' routines don't go to AI — The app itself uses a child's nap and bedtime to block out rest time. They are never sent to the AI model.

Plan the trip

  1. Plan a trip — Tap Plan a trip on the Today tab or in Ask the family. Pick where, when and who's going, then tap Make plan. A trip can be up to 5 days.
  2. Read it day by day — The plan has Schedule, Packing, Budget and Roles tabs. The schedule includes rest and meal times from your daily rhythm, and each place comes with Find in map app and an alternative.
  3. Check what's marked — Opening hours, prices and travel times, which AI can't know for sure, are marked Needs checking. Confirm them from each place's official information before you go.
  4. Every adult on the trip accepts — A plan is added to the calendar, to-dos and the trip card only after every participating adult accepts. If anyone declines, nothing changes, and you can adjust it and make it again.

A plan only uses records every participating adult can see. At first only the participating adults see the plan; with Show to the whole family on, the whole family can, once the other adults turn it on too.

PlanAI uses
Weekend plan2
1 to 3 day trip3
4 or 5 day trip4
Redo one trip day1

The free plan's 5 AI uses a month cover one 1 to 3 day trip plan plus 2 questions. If a plan can't be made, the uses are given back.

Packing: what you forgot last time comes first

The Packing tab splits kids' and adults' things and shows why each item is there (age group, routine, general suggestion and so on). The most useful part is your last trip.

  1. Mark items after the trip — When you're back, mark each item Used, Forgot or Not needed.
  2. See it next time — In the next trip plan, items you marked Forgot come first, tagged Forgotten last trip.
  3. See who packs what — Each packing group shows who has it, or that no one is assigned yet. The Roles tab suggests how to split the jobs.

The Budget tab works the same way: amounts come from your last trip, what you type in, then AI estimates, and estimates are marked for checking. The app adds up the total.

Lighter plans for the weekend

For a weekend close to home, use Plan the weekend. It gives two options for each free slot, fitted to your family's free time and daily rhythm. Pick one per slot and accept.

After the trip: group events and photos into an album

Trip photos end up scattered across everyone's phones. AXFamily's family memories groups a trip's events and photos so the family can look back together.

  1. Add photos — On the Photos tab, make a New album or tap Add photos in one. Only a smaller copy with the location removed is uploaded; the original stays on your phone.
  2. Check AI suggestions — Once a week the app looks through family records and suggests trip and photo groupings, such as "Make an album 'Autumn camping' from 9 photos" or "Add 3 events or tasks to a trip". Open AI suggestions on the Family tab; nothing changes until you tap Review and save, and only you see the suggestions.
  3. Open the trip card — The trip's events, to-dos and album come together on one trip card. From the album, Open trip card takes you back to that trip's plans.
  4. Ask later — In Ask the family, ask "When was our beach trip last year?". It answers from your records and shows which one it used, and says so when nothing matches.

Family memories use only records from adults who agreed to AI. Names and notes of children under 14 are never sent to AI, and album suggestions don't count toward AI uses.

What it can't do

  • It isn't a place-recommendation service. A plan is a draft fitted to your family's schedule and rhythm. Check opening hours, prices and bookings yourself.
  • It doesn't book or pay. Book stays and restaurants with each service directly.
  • Photo storage has a limit. 1,000 photos on the free plan and 10,000 with Family Plus. They are small copies for the family to look at, not full-quality backups.
  • AI can be wrong. Plans and suggestions are labeled "AI-generated", and you can report odd results in the app.

FAQ

How long a trip can it plan?

Up to 5 days at a time. A weekend plan uses 2 AI uses, a 1 to 3 day trip 3, and a 4 or 5 day trip 4.

What if another adult declines the plan?

If anyone declines, nothing goes into the calendar, to-dos or trip card. You can adjust the plan and make it again.

Is my child's nap time sent to AI?

No. The app uses a child's daily rhythm itself to set rest time, and doesn't send it to AI.

Are original photos uploaded?

No. The phone uploads a smaller copy with the location removed. The original stays on your phone.

Related articles

  • Share a family calendar and decide who does what
  • School notices and class schedules in one calendar

About AXFamily

A shared family calendar for Android that gathers your family's events and to-dos in one place and shows who's on each one. It includes a trip and weekend helper and family memories.

item.title: School notices and class schedules in one calendar – SugarMount
item.description:
Help · Android

School notices and class schedules in one calendar

Kids' plans arrive on paper notices, in school apps and as texts from after-school classes. Here is how to pull out the dates and things to bring, put them in one family calendar, and decide who handles each.

This guide is based on AXFamily 1.2.0, an Android app by SugarMount. Every school, name and event in the text and screens is made up. AXFamily isn't made by a school, so you add the notices you receive yourself.

Where kids' plans come from

SourceWhat's in itHow to add it
Paper school noticeEvent dates, things to bring, reply deadlinesTake a photo, then Add
School app messageHomework, supplies, tomorrow's planTake a screenshot, then Add
Class texts or PDFsTime changes, make-up classes, closuresScreenshot or PDF, then Add
The same class every weekDay and timeOne repeating event

When only the person who got the notice knows what's in it, the others easily miss a reply deadline or something to bring. One habit is enough: whoever receives it adds it right away and picks who takes care of it.

Turn a school notice photo into events

  1. Add — Tap Add at the bottom of the Today, Calendar or Records tab and choose Photos & screenshots or File (PDF). The app only receives the photos you pick in the photo picker.
  2. Pick who's in it — Under People in this item, choose the family members the notice is about. A notice about a child can go to AI only after a guardian's consent is confirmed.
  3. Organize with AI — Each notice photo or PDF page uses 1 AI use. It's usually done within 15 seconds, and the result also shows up in your Inbox.
  4. Review suggestions — The dates and to-dos the AI found appear as suggestions. Compare dates and times with the original and fix anything wrong. You can ask a family member to take a reply or a supplies list right on this screen.
  5. Save — Nothing is saved until you check it. Until then only you can see it; when you save, you choose whether to share it with the family.

The first time you open the app, See a sample notice walks through this with a sample newsletter:

"Grade 3 field trip on Oct 17. Please arrive by 8:40 AM. Bring: lunch box, water, picnic mat. Please hand in the sign-up form to the homeroom teacher by next Tuesday."

The sample screen shows "Grade 3 field trip (Oct 17 · 8:40 AM)" and "Pack field trip supplies (lunch box, water, picnic mat)" as items to check, and "Hand in the sign-up form" as an item that needs a date, quoting "by next Tuesday" from the original. The sample is never saved.

Weekly classes as repeating events

A class at the same time every week doesn't need a photo each time. Add it once as a repeating event.

  1. Add event — Enter a title (say, Seoa's swim class), the day and the time.
  2. Repeat — Choose every week and an end date. For a school term, use the last day of term; if you can't say, choose no end.
  3. With — Add the child. If no adult is going along, the Sunday heads-up lists it as "No one to go along", and you can tap I'll do it right there.
  4. Change one day only — For a make-up class or a closure, edit just that day. When you edit a repeating event, the app asks whether to change this event only or the whole series.

Got a text about a time change? Take a screenshot and use Add. Check the date before saving here too.

Replies and supplies as to-dos, with an owner

What slips through most often isn't the event date but the reply deadline and things to bring. Make them to-dos rather than events, and give each one an owner.

  • Supplies as a checklist. Inside a "Pack field trip supplies" to-do, add lunch box, water and picnic mat as checklist items and tick them off as you pack.
  • Replies with a due date. Give "Hand in the sign-up form" a due date, and you'll get a reminder as it gets close.
  • One owner. When you ask someone to take a to-do, they answer with I'll do it or Can't do it. Anything nobody took is collected under No one assigned in the Sunday heads-up.

Before you use AI to organize notices

  • AI can be wrong. Everything it makes is labeled "AI-generated". Always check relative dates such as "next Tuesday" and times against the original.
  • Each adult decides. AI turns on only for adults who give their own consent. Without AI, Type it in creates the same events and to-dos.
  • There are limits. The free plan has 5 AI uses a month, shared by the family and refilled on the 1st. There are daily limits too (20 per person, 30 per family).
  • Only a small copy is sent. The phone shrinks the photo and removes its location before sending. The original stays on your phone.
  • Children's information gets extra care. A notice about a child is read by AI only with a guardian's consent. For items without a child, you confirm there is no child's name, face or contact info before sending.

For the details, see the AXFamily privacy policy.

FAQ

Does it connect to my school's app?

No. AXFamily isn't made by a school and doesn't connect to school apps. Take a screenshot of the message and use Add.

How many AI uses does one notice photo take?

One photo is 1 use, and each PDF page is 1 use. If AI fails to answer, the uses are given back (up to 4 a month).

Can I organize notices without AI?

Yes. Choose Type it in under Add, or add events and to-dos yourself. Events, to-dos and reminders all work without AI.

Does my whole family see the notices I add?

They start private. Share them with the family when you save, or change who can see them later to pick specific people.

Related articles

  • Share a family calendar and decide who does what
  • Plan a trip around naps, then keep photos together

About AXFamily

A shared family calendar for Android that gathers your family's events and to-dos in one place and shows who's on each one. Upload a photo of a school notice, and AI finds its dates and things to bring.

Get AXFamily on Google PlayAbout the AXFamily app

See the AXFamily terms of service.

item.title: Install Claude Code on Windows: Git to first run – SugarMount
item.description:
AX notes · How-to

Install Claude Code on Windows: Git to first run

Claude Code installs on Windows with one line pasted into PowerShell, and it does not need an administrator window. Install Git from its official download page first.

Windows harness series, part 3 of 11 · Previous Before you start: PowerShell · Next Log in and ask a first unattended question

This part installs two programs. Claude Code is the AI program that does the work in this series. Git for Windows brings along a tool Claude Code uses to run commands. When both are in, a fresh PowerShell window prints their version numbers.

Use the Windows PowerShell window from part 2, and copy and paste commands the same way.

When you finish this part

  • Result: in a new PowerShell window, git --version and claude --version print versions, and claude doctor reports No installation issues found.
  • You need: part 2 (opening PowerShell), Windows 10 1809 or later, an internet connection, 4 GB of RAM or more
  • Cost: nothing to pay in this part. To use Claude Code you sign in with a paid plan in part 4; the free plan does not include Claude Code.

Step 1: Download Git for Windows

Git for Windows installs Git Bash, a command shell. When Git Bash is present, Claude Code runs commands through its Bash tool; without it, Claude Code falls back to its PowerShell tool. The official docs call Git recommended, not required. This series installs it so that every reader follows the same path.

  1. Open the official Git for Windows download page in your browser: https://git-scm.com/install/windows

  2. Under the Windows tab, click Click here to download in the first line.

  3. If your PC has an ARM64 processor, click Git for Windows/ARM64 Setup. instead.

It worked if

Your browser downloads an installer. On 2026-11-11 the link pointed to Git-2.56.1-64-bit.exe; the number follows whatever the latest release is on the day you download.

Step 2: Install Git and check it

The installer offers several choices, and none of them needs changing for this series. The download page does not walk through those screens, so this guide does not describe them one by one either.

  1. Run the installer you downloaded. You'll find it in your browser's downloads list or in your Downloads folder.

  2. If a Windows confirmation box (User Account Control) appears, click Yes.

  3. Leave the settings as they are and click Next through the screens, then Install. When it finishes, click Finish.

  4. Close any PowerShell window you already had open and open Windows PowerShell again, as in part 2. A window opened before the install may not find the new program.

  5. Run this command.

    git --version

It worked if

You get a line that starts with git version. On the PC this series was written on it read git version 2.45.2.windows.1; a fresh download shows a higher number.

Step 3: Run the Claude Code install command

Installing Claude Code takes one line in PowerShell. The command comes from the official setup page: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup

  1. Open a Windows PowerShell window. It does not have to be an admin window; the official docs say you do not need to run as Administrator.

  2. Copy the command below, paste it, and press Enter. It is the same command as in the box under Windows PowerShell: on the official page; scroll down the page a little to see that box.

    irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex

  3. Wait. The official docs say the command shows no progress while it downloads Claude Code. Leave the window open even if it looks stuck.

The first half, irm, fetches the install script from the internet, and the second half, iex, runs what was fetched. That is why you paste the whole line, including iex.

It worked if

The command finishes and a new prompt line starting with PS appears. If the output mentions Setup notes:, do step 4 and then step 5 as well.

Running into the same problem? Email us what you are seeing and we will reply. Email us

Step 4: Check the install in a new window

The window you installed from may not find the claude command yet. The official docs also tell you to open a new terminal window before checking.

  1. Close PowerShell and open Windows PowerShell again.

  2. Check the version.

    claude --version

  3. Run the diagnostics. claude doctor does not start a session; it only reads and reports the state of the install and your settings.

    claude doctor

It worked if

claude --version prints a number followed by (Claude Code), like 2.1.322 (Claude Code), and the claude doctor output includes No installation issues found.

Three lines in claude doctor are worth reading. Running: native means Claude Code was installed the officially recommended way. Path: shows where claude.exe lives: the .local\bin folder inside your user folder. Auto-updates: enabled means updates are on. A native install downloads updates in the background, and the new version takes effect the next time you start Claude Code.

A line starting Managed settings (remote): not fetched is normal on a personal plan. The line right below it, Organization policy: not applicable to individual subscription plans, says why: company-managed settings do not apply to individual plans, so nothing was fetched.

Step 5: Fix PATH if you saw Setup notes

Do this step only if the step 3 output showed Setup notes: with a sentence ending in .local\bin is not in your PATH. Otherwise skip it.

PATH is the list of folders Windows searches when you type a program's name. It is stored as a per-user setting called an environment variable. The installer does not edit that list itself; it only prints the warning and the fix.

  1. Paste these two lines one at a time, pressing Enter after each. The first reads your current list; the second adds the Claude Code folder to the end and saves it.

    $currentPath = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('PATH', 'User')
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('PATH', "$currentPath;$env:USERPROFILE\.local\bin", 'User')

  2. Close PowerShell and open a new window. The change only applies to windows opened afterwards.

  3. Run claude --version again.

It worked if

As in step 4, the version number is followed by (Claude Code).

If you get stuck

If you seeWhyDo this
'irm' is not recognized as an internal or external commandYou pasted into CMDPaste it into a Windows PowerShell window
The token '&&' is not a valid statement separatorYou pasted the CMD command into PowerShellUse the irm command from step 3
A message containing The term 'claude' is not recognizedThe window predates the install, or the folder is missing from PATHTry a new window; if it persists, do step 5
Claude Code does not support 32-bit WindowsYou opened the (x86) PowerShellOpen Windows PowerShell without (x86)
A message ending in because it is being used by another processAnother process is holding the install filesRun Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\.claude\downloads", then repeat step 3
Script text scrolls past and nothing installsThe | iex part at the end of the line was missingPaste the whole line again: irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex

Windows harness series: all 11 parts

  • 1. What a harness is
  • 2. Before you start: PowerShell
  • 3. Install Git and Claude Code
  • 4. Log in and ask a first unattended question
  • 5. Install Docker Desktop
  • 6. Download the kit and run a first job
  • 7. Schedule it to run every day
  • 8. A morning GA4 report job
  • 9. Ad budget checks and approvals
  • 10. Planning TikTok, Reels and Shorts
  • 11. Two weeks of running it, and the safeguards

Next: Log in and ask a first unattended question

Questions or ideas?

Send us where you got stuck applying this, a question about the numbers, or a topic you would like covered.

Email us sugarmount21@gmail.com

FAQ

Can I install Claude Code without Git?

Without Git for Windows, Claude Code still installs and runs commands through its PowerShell tool instead of the Bash tool. This series installs Git so that everyone follows the same steps.

Can I install it with winget instead?

The official docs list winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode too, but a winget install does not update itself; you have to run winget upgrade Anthropic.ClaudeCode now and then. This series uses the step 3 method, which updates automatically.

Do I need to open PowerShell as administrator?

The Claude Code docs say you run the install command from PowerShell or CMD and do not need to run as Administrator.

As of 2026-11-12. The official Git for Windows download page, Claude Code setup and install troubleshooting docs (checked 2026-11-11), and output run on the PC this series was written on.

This note is written from values SugarMount measured itself; an AI coding agent was used to draft it.

More AX notes

  • "6.7" < "6.11" is false: comparing Remote Config versions as strings froze content updates
  • A launch crash only on Android 7: one java.time call in a shared module and a NewApi lint gate

All AX notes

item.title: Measuring 4.5:1 colour contrast in the site build – SugarMount
item.description:
AX notes · Measurement

4.5:1 contrast in the site build: the dark hover pair that failed for 7 of 11 apps

A contrast rule that lives in one sentence of a doc does not hold. Our site build computes 11 contrast pairs per app and fails if any pair drops below 4.5:1.

Measuring text contrast 3/3

On a site where each app has its own accent colour, every colour change shifts the contrast of buttons, badges and link text along with it. This site started with one sentence as its rule: white text on the accent must reach 4.5:1. When we reworked the design system in October 2026 and measured again, the hovered outline button in dark mode fell below 4.5:1 for 7 of our 11 apps. Now the build computes 11 contrast pairs per app and fails if any falls short. Below: what that gate catches, what it still misses, and the steps to build the same gate.

Dark hover contrast at the October rework: 4.17 to 4.66

Each app on this site has a single accent hex in data/apps.json. sds_apps.py computes nine colour tokens from it as CSS text, and build.py writes that to a file. In dark mode the pale background bg-accent-weak is 24% accent mixed into the default dark surface #172131. The dark text colour fg-accent is the accent with its HSL lightness raised 1% at a time until it reaches 4.6:1 on #1D2940, the lightest of the three dark neutral surfaces.

Put fg-accent text on bg-accent-weak, as a hovered outline button would, and the 11 apps at the October 18 rework score: Arrow Knots 4.17, SugarSpeller 4.20, Compress Image 4.27, Flip & Rotate Image 4.31, SugarCard 4.40, SugarAlbum 4.41, AXFamily 4.41, Block Turn 4.58, SugarClip 4.59, Convert Image 4.64, SugarDoc 4.66. Seven are under 4.5 and nine under 4.6.

Our working notes say a review agent checking the design spec flagged this pair: "7 of 11 apps, lowest 4.17". We could not find the review itself, so we recomputed it from the app list at the rework and got the same numbers. The implementation commit already shipped the fixed pairing: in site.css, .button--outline:hover uses fg-accent-contrast for its text and border.

For 13 days the rule was one line of prose

The commit that first added the site pages, on 20 September 2026, set the default accent in site.css to #00897B ("default accent: SugarCompress"). The same day, the first commit of the utilities app repository listed "compress (temp) #00897B" in its design tokens. Both commits carry an AI co-author trailer. White text on that colour is 4.32:1, and the colour as text on the light background #F6F8FB is 4.06:1.

The next day, the "Design v2" commit in the utilities repository (also AI co-authored) caught it. Its design spec reads "temporary #00897B (4.3:1, fails AA) is replaced by #0F766E.", and another section makes 4.5:1 text contrast in both themes a principle. The site picked up #0F766E (white text 5.47:1) on 5 October, when a commit introduced data/apps.json.

The contrast rule that commit added to AGENTS.md was a field description: accent "(hex, white text on it must reach 4.5:1)". Searching that commit's tools/build.py for lumin, contrast or 4.5 finds nothing.

The first assumption matched the line: if white text clears 4.5:1 on the accent, the accent is safe. But one accent becomes nine tokens per theme, and those tokens meet as text and background in 11 pairs. Today every white-on-accent pair across the 13 apps is 5.45:1 or higher, while the dark hover pair from the same accents goes down to 4.17.

The dark accent was tuned against a different background

The dark hover used fg-accent for text and bg-accent-weak for the background. fg-accent only guarantees 4.6:1 on #1D2940 (relative luminance 0.0222), and for the blue and teal apps the pale background is lighter than that. Arrow Knots' bg-accent-weak, #14344E, has a luminance of 0.0315, and the same text colour #0A99EE falls from 4.71 to 4.17. The purple and magenta apps passed because their pale backgrounds sit close to #1D2940: Convert Image (#2C2359, 0.0246) at 4.64 and SugarDoc (#32223C, 0.0215) at 4.66.

A second assumption, made while writing this note, was that raising the target to 4.6 would cover the hover too, but the 4.6 target is measured on #1D2940, so with today's formula the pair on the pale background is still 4.17.

The fix is a token per pair. fg-accent-contrast takes the dark accent and lightens it again, 1% at a time, until it reaches 4.6:1 on the pale background. For Arrow Knots that moves #0A99EE to #17A2F5 and 4.17 to 4.61. The header of sds_apps.py states the rule as T2: "text on bg-accent-weak is fg-accent-contrast".

Running into the same problem? Email us what you are seeing and we will reply. Email us

The gate computes 11 pairs per app, 143 today

Inside python tools/build.py --check, which AGENTS.md says to run before every commit, sds_gates() checks three things. The rest of that check is described in Keeping a static site safe when several AI agents edit it: one --check before every commit.

  • for each app, 11 pairs; any pair under 4.5:1 is an error, SDS contrast <app>: <pair names>. Pairs have names like white on accent, accent on basement and d-contrast on d-weak; the full list of 11 is in audit();
  • the tokens read back from the generated assets/sds-apps.css must equal what accent_tokens() computes (rule T1: a literal hex per app);
  • the header mark colours in site.css must match the social-image generator og.py.

The docstring explains the 4.6 target: "targets are 4.6:1 so rounding and browser blending never drop below 4.5:1". Every mix and lightness step rounds RGB to integers. Because of that margin, Block Turn (4.58) and SugarClip (4.59) also got their own token, and in the dark block of the generated CSS at the rework, 9 of 11 apps declare a separate fg-accent-contrast.

We also ran a revert test. Setting Compress Image back to #00897B in the copy's apps.json made the gate print this (run with --check on 3 November, confirmed through audit() on 4 November):

error: SDS contrast sugarcompress: white on accent, accent on basement
1 gate error(s)

Two apps arrived later, CarDrawer (19 October) and TrimBox (31 October). Each added one hex to apps.json, and the colour code did not change through 4 November. The gate then computed 13 apps x 11 pairs = 143 pairs. As of 4 November, had the hover kept fg-accent, 9 of the 13 would have been under 4.5, with TrimBox at 4.22 and CarDrawer at 4.39.

Update, 13 November 2026: a site-wide colour refresh that day changed the dark neutral surfaces (the darkest is now #0E1217), and the tokens were recomputed by the same functions. After the refresh the lowest of the 143 pairs is AXFamily's dark accent text at 4.60:1. Had the hover kept fg-accent, 3 of 13 apps would now be under 4.5 (Compress Image and Arrow Knots at 4.39, Flip & Rotate Image at 4.48). Because the gate recomputes from the same formula, no colour had to be fixed by hand.

Swap the CSS pairing and the gate still passes

On 3 November we changed the site.css in a copy of the site so the hover text was var(--sds-fg-accent) again, rebuilt, and ran --check, which printed up to date; gates passed with the 4.17:1 pair back in the stylesheet. The only thing sds_gates() reads from site.css is the header mark regex; contrast comes entirely from the token pairs listed in audit().

As of 4 November, site.css used bg-accent-weak as the background in six rules.

SelectorText tokenIn the gate's pairs?
.app-tile:hoverfg-accent-contrastYes
.button--outline:hoverfg-accent-contrastYes
.badgefg-accent-contrastYes
.trust lifg-accent-contrastYes
[data-app] .notebody text fg-neutralNo
.ax-ctanot setNo

On app pages, .note keeps fg-neutral body text (its border, links and the eyebrow use fg-accent-contrast), and .ax-cta sets no text colour at all. Neither pair is among the 11, so neither is measured. We left both unfixed; that call belongs to whoever owns the build.

Both the mistakes and the catches in this history are recorded in AI co-authored commits or agent work. The spec rule that a new accent should be at least dE00 12 (a colour-distance measure) from existing ones was left out of the gate because "the new-key dE00 >= 12 rule needs a human to know which key is new"; the CLI only warns about pairs under dE00 8, currently 7 (smallest 2.2, Flip & Rotate Image and Arrow Knots).

color-mix() is banned by T3, and dark colours are not hand-picked

Letting the browser blend hover colours with CSS color-mix() is banned by rule T3. The gate compares literal hex values in the generated CSS with computed ones, and a browser-blended colour gives it nothing to compare. Hand-picking dark colours per app was dropped too: the site went from 11 apps to 13, and that approach means a person picking nine tokens for every new app.

We measured rendered pixels in another app; that write-up is Our contrast checker passed while skipping 40% of the text. sds_apps.py uses only the Python standard library and never starts a browser.

Without design tokens, with colours written per component, there is no pair list to compute in the first place. Gradients, text over photos and translucent layers don't reduce to two tokens, and this site doesn't measure them either.

From one accent hex to a 143-pair gate in six steps

  1. Keep one accent hex per brand or app in your source data and derive every other token with a function.
  2. Write down every text-on-background pair. Then search the CSS for rules that use each background token (grep -n "accent-weak" assets/site.css) and check each rule's text token against your list, as in the table above.
  3. Aim a little above 4.5 (we use 4.6), and give any pair that falls short its own token.
  4. Fail the build check when any pair is under 4.5:1, and compare the generated CSS values with the computed ones.
  5. Put an old failing colour into apps.json and run python tools/build.py --check: expect a line containing 1 gate error(s), and a line containing up to date; gates passed again once you revert. Then deliberately mismatch a CSS pairing, rebuild with build.py and run --check. Here it still says gates passed.
  6. Run python tools/sds_apps.py to print the colour-distance warnings and have a person look; today it lists 7 pairs under dE00 8.

Don't leave a contrast rule as a sentence in a doc. Make the build compute it from a list of colour pairs, and check that the list matches the pairs your CSS actually uses. We have only done the first half. The next step is a --check stage that extracts the text token of every rule with a bg-accent-weak background and compares it with the 11 pairs, and before that, measuring the .note body text and the .ax-cta text for the first time.

Questions or ideas?

Send us where you got stuck applying this, a question about the numbers, or a topic you would like covered.

Email us sugarmount21@gmail.com

Measuring text contrast: all 3 parts

  1. Our contrast checker passed while skipping 40% of the text: make it print how much it measured

This is the last part.

FAQ

Which text does the WCAG 4.5:1 contrast minimum apply to?

Normal-size text. WCAG 2 success criterion 1.4.3 sets 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text. Our gate ignores text size and applies 4.5:1 to all 11 pairs.

How is a contrast ratio calculated?

Take the relative luminance of both colours, L1 for the lighter and L2 for the darker, and compute (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05). Relative luminance linearises the sRGB channels and sums 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B. The contrast() function in sds_apps.py is this formula.

Sources: the site repository's git history and its colour-token module (tools/sds_apps.py), and the design docs in our utilities app repository. Ratios were recomputed on 3 and 4 November 2026 in a copy of the site with that module's functions; the values after the 13 November refresh and the live screenshot are from that day.

This note is written from values SugarMount measured itself; an AI coding agent was used to draft it.

  • Claude Code on WSL vs native Windows: what changed after the move

item.title: Gemini in an Android app: cost, eval, daily caps – SugarMount
item.description:
AX Notes · Measurement

The first LLM feature in a spell-check app: cost, model evaluation and daily caps for "Why is this wrong?"

Adding an LLM to an app means choosing a model, a billing path and a spending cap. Our spelling app picked its model with a 59-case eval, and its server function stops calling the LLM after 3,000 calls a day.

Adding an LLM to an app 1/4

The first eval run on the night of September 27, 2026 failed on all 59 calls with HTTP 402. It used an AI Studio key that the coding agent had said around noon that day would be billed against our Firebase credit, and we were in the middle of giving our Korean spelling app SugarSpeller its first server function and LLM. After the key was replaced with Vertex AI, gemini-3.8-flash gave a correct reason for all 59 corrections (the right rule for 54), with a p95 latency of 4.3 seconds and a cost of $0.93 per 1,000 calls. In the two weeks after the October 1 release, 3.7% of users who ran a check tapped the button; among users who had opened the correction sheet, it was 41%.

Sources: the design doc in the app repository (approved 2026-09-27), git history, the release decision log and the work log. Usage is from GA4; cost is from the usage records the function writes (checked 2026-11-02, times in UTC+9).

The 59-case eval: flash-lite at 78%, 3.8-flash at 100%

The feature explains one correction at a time: the user taps a corrected word and gets a one-line reason plus the name of the Korean orthography rule behind it. We picked the model with 59 corrections taken from real checker responses stored as test fixtures in the app: 38 from Naver's spell checker and 21 from Daum's (Naver and Daum are the two big Korean portals, and the app uses their checkers). The pass mark was written into the design doc before the run: at least 90% correct and a p95 of 2.5 seconds or less. Every call went to the Vertex AI global endpoint.

Model (prompt)Reason correctRule also correctp50 / p95Per 1,000
gemini-3.5-flash-lite (v1)43/59 (73%)30/591.06 s / 1.26 s$0.27
gemini-3.5-flash-lite (v2)46/59 (78%)38/591.08 s / 4.6 s$0.42
gemini-3.8-flash (v2)59/59 (100%)54/59 (92%)2.0 s / 4.3 s$0.93

Prompt v2 added an order of checks for spacing errors and a table of reasons for the most common corrections. It moved flash-lite from 73% to 78% and no further. Its wrong answers included explaining a noun fused with hada ("to do") as an ending or particle, garbled syllables, and calling an archaic spelling of a polite ending a past tense. 3.8-flash made no typos; its five misses were all wrong rule citations. It costs more than twice as much as flash-lite v2 per 1,000 calls, and it was the only model over the 90% bar, so it became the default.

The first 3.8-flash run returned 59 empty answers. The model's thinking tokens used up the 160-token output limit before any JSON came out; setting thinkingBudget: 0 fixed it. The 2.5-second target was missed. This model is served only from the global endpoint (the Seoul and Tokyo regions returned 404), and each call took 2.1 to 2.8 seconds. Because that was still inside the app's 8-second timeout and the button shows a progress indicator, the design doc moved the target to a p95 of 5 seconds.

The AI Studio key never touched the $300 credit

The 402 came from billing. The error read Your prepayment credits are depleted, and authentication had succeeded. In this project, AI Studio billing was prepaid only, so it had no link to the 90-day $300 free-trial credit (held in Cloud Billing) that came with moving the Firebase project to the pay-as-you-go Blaze plan.

At 12:01 the agent wrote that with the $300 credit, paid-tier Gemini API usage would be billed to the same project, and ten minutes later it produced a table showing the credit applied to both. The spec switched to keyless Vertex AI at 12:18, then at 12:21 went back to an AI Studio key the operator had already created, on the grounds that it shared the billing account.

The function, the quota code and the cache were all tested against a fake provider during the day, so the first real Gemini call was the eval run around 10 p.m. When the agent reported the 402 at 22:04, its first recommendation was to buy AI Studio prepaid credit (minimum $5). At 22:06 the operator asked why, if the $300 was supposed to cover it. The agent then said its earlier explanation was wrong: AI Studio keys used to bill a project's Cloud billing account after the fact, and this project didn't work that way.

A commit at 22:10 moved Gemini authentication to Vertex AI with ADC (Application Default Credentials, the service account the code already runs as). Vertex bills through Cloud Billing, which per the design doc is where the credit applies, and there is no API key to store or rotate. The deploy 49 minutes later hit one more snag: declaring an unused secret on the function was enough to make the deploy query Secret Manager and fail with 403, so the secret is now declared only in key mode.

Before building an LLM feature, make one real call and check which bill it lands on. A 200 response does not say which balance paid for it. After the move to Vertex, this app computed its cost from token counts the function records times the list price, and the repository has no record of the credit deduction being checked against a billing report.

The function refuses LLM calls past 3,000 a day

explainCorrection is a single callable function on Cloud Functions for Firebase (2nd gen). The app signs in anonymously when its process opens the first screen, and the Firebase SDK attaches the auth token to each call. The function validates input, checks the cache, takes from the quota, calls the LLM, then stores the result. The cache comes before the quota, so an explanation that already exists costs the user nothing.

ControlDefaultHow to change it
Free quota5 a day per anonymous uidFirestore doc config/limits (cached 60 s)
Subscriber ceiling100 a day per uidSame doc
Global cap3,000 LLM attempts a daySame doc; 0 closes it
App Check enforcementOff (measured only); current setting unconfirmedrequireAppCheck in the same doc
Button in the appOnRemote Config explain_enabled = false

The day rolls over at midnight Korea time. The day key is computed by adding nine hours to UTC milliseconds rather than trusting the server's time zone. The global cap counts LLM attempts, not requests: retries and hedged duplicates each count, and only attempts that failed before billing (network errors and the like) are given back. Timeouts stay counted, because the provider may already have charged for them.

A budget alert sends an email and does not stop charges, which is why the design doc calls the 3,000-call cap the real safeguard. At the eval price ($0.93), a full day at the cap is about $2.8; with the longer v3 prompt from September 28 (about $1.1 per 1,000) it is about $3.3 by our calculation. A call cap works as a money cap only because each call is bounded: the original and corrected words are limited to 60 code points each, and the output to 160 tokens. The agent's morning estimate (under 0.1 won per call, under 1,000 won a month) used flash-lite prices; the chosen model costs 3.4 times flash-lite v1 per 1,000 calls.

In the first release stage the function trusts the app's claim that the user subscribes. A forged claim buys 95 extra explanations a day at under 10 won (well under a cent), so receipt checks were deferred. Putting the daily total document in the same transaction as the user's quota made concurrent requests die on lock timeouts, and on September 28 the total moved outside the transaction. As a result, the global cap can overshoot by the number of requests in flight.

Remote Config refreshed only on the launcher screen, and people who used only the mini window (opened from text selection in another app) never pass through it, so switching off explain_enabled would have left their button in place. The September 29 release review caught it, and the mini window now fetches config before it opens the sheet.

A 7.9-second cold start pushed the app timeout to 15 seconds

The smoke test after the production deploy on the night of September 27 measured 7.9 seconds for the first call and 1.6 to 3.0 seconds after that. The function runs with zero minimum instances, and the app's timeout was 8 seconds, so a cold call came within 0.1 seconds of it. So the app timeout went up to 15 seconds. Keeping one instance warm (about $3 to $4 a month) stayed in the function docs as a fallback if cold starts became a problem. LLM calls on October 26 and 27 cost $0.020 in total, so the warm instance would cost far more than the feature itself.

The next day, one repeated eval call that stretched to 44.5 seconds set the server-side deadlines: 6 seconds per attempt and 12 for the whole request. From October 25 the function hedges: if an attempt is silent for 4 seconds, it sends the same request again and takes whichever answers first. Failures went from 16 of 25 in the October 24 function log to 0 of 16 on October 26 and 27.

Running into the same problem? Email us what you are seeing and we will reply. Email us

3.7% of checking users, 41% of sheet openers

The decision rule went into the decision log before release. Fourteen days in, if 8% or more of users who ran a check tapped the button, keep it; under 3%, test a new position and wording. The October 17 review (October 2 to 16, app 1.6.025 or later) counted 56 of 1,527 checking users, 3.7%, with 77 requests. That sits between the two thresholds.

Over the same period, 138 users (9.0%) tapped a corrected word to open the sheet, and 56 of them pressed the button. 41% of people who reached the sheet wanted the reason, so the bottleneck was finding the sheet rather than the button. Version 1.6.031, rolled out in stages from October 18, added a one-time hint that the highlighted words can be tapped.

With about 8 requests a day, the 14-day cache hit rate was 11% against a 40% target. How the shared cache key was built is covered in the blind A/B that let us stop sending context to the LLM.

Mass-created anonymous accounts hit only the global cap

A uid's quota starts over when the app is reinstalled. A script that keeps creating anonymous accounts makes the per-user limit of 5 meaningless; what remains is the global 3,000 and App Check, which defaults to measuring only. If one explanation were expensive, verify the subscription on the server from day one.

The 59 cases came only from the checkers' red, green and blue groups (Naver red 25, green 13; Daum red 14, green 5, blue 2); there was not one purple or violet case, and the September 27 scoring was done by the same agent that wrote the code. No human scored it. A model that lives only on the global endpoint also changes what a privacy policy can say about where data is processed; another of our apps ran into that with the same model, written up in the privacy-policy note on AI processing location.

Adding the same feature to your app

  1. Make one real model call through a path that bills to Cloud Billing (Vertex AI here). On 402 or 403, stop and settle the billing path first. On 200, check the billing report for the credit deduction.
  2. Pull about 50 cases from your app's test data and put accuracy, p95 and cost per 1,000 calls for each candidate in one table. Write the pass mark first, and set the thinking budget of thinking models to 0.
  3. Expose one callable function that requires anonymous auth, with three limits (free per user, subscriber ceiling, global) keyed by day in your users' time zone. Keep the limits in a document you can change without a deploy, with 0 meaning closed.
  4. Cap input length and output tokens.
  5. Give the app a remote switch that hides the button, and check that every entry screen refreshes it.
  6. After the production deploy, time the first call to a cold instance and set the app timeout above it. Before release, write the decision rule: two usage thresholds, cache hit rate, failure rate and daily cost.

The default limits and the thinking switch (MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS is 160):

// default limits
export const DEFAULT_LIMITS: Limits = { freePerDay: 5, entitledPerDay: 100, globalPerDay: 3000, requireAppCheck: false };
// Gemini generateContent config, in part
maxOutputTokens: MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS,
thinkingConfig: { thinkingBudget: 0 },

Still open: usage after the tap hint, and a price doubling

The tap hint in 1.6.031 is judged by whether 6% or more of users who saw it request an explanation. The review was due November 1, and as of November 2 the log has no row for it yet. 3.8-flash is scheduled to double in price on January 1, 2027, to $1.50 input and $7.50 output per million tokens; on that day the prices and the worst-day figure need recalculating. We also haven't seen a real bill yet, since the 90-day credit is still running.

Questions or ideas?

Send us where you got stuck applying this, a question about the numbers, or a topic you would like covered.

Email us sugarmount21@gmail.com

Adding an LLM to an app: all 4 parts

  1. A shared LLM cache could have frozen a prompt injection: the blind A/B that let us stop sending context

FAQ

Can Firebase Blaze credit pay for the Gemini API?

Per the design doc, only Vertex AI is on the credit path in this project; we haven't confirmed it on an invoice yet. The AI Studio key was on prepaid-only billing, so all 59 eval calls on September 27, 2026 were rejected with 402.

How do you cap the cost of an LLM feature?

Count LLM calls inside the function and refuse them past a daily limit. A budget alert only sends an email. This app closes at 3,000 calls a day, and one Firestore document can change that number or set it to 0 without a deploy.

This note is written from values SugarMount measured itself; an AI coding agent was used to draft it.

More AX notes

  • Three agent designs, three judges: the market judge alone would have picked the one that crashed on every KakaoTalk file
  • Verifying an AI agent's "done" report: 95.2% vs a 92.3% cap
