item.title: VIBRATE crash and the fresh-install monkey test – SugarMount
item.description:
AX notes · Incident

The agent said it was tested. The game crashed on the first tutorial tap: a missing VIBRATE permission and the fresh-install monkey test

Scripted device tests missed a crash caused by one missing permission line. Running adb monkey on a freshly cleared app reproduced it at the 15th of 800 events.

When green does not mean tested 1/6

Our AI coding agent reported an Android game as crash-free, and it died the first time a person tapped it. One permission line was missing from the manifest, and the agent's check had been nothing more than launching the app. A crash like this shows up when you clear the app's data, run adb monkey (Android's built-in random-tap tool) and pass or fail the run on the crash count. Below are that script and the reasons the existing tests missed the bug.

On the night of October 1, 2026, the agent installed a pre-release build of the puzzle game Arrow Knots on a Galaxy S24 and reported "launched in 857 ms, no crash". Four minutes later the operator reported an error in the tutorial: the app closed on the first arrow tap. The fix landed 5 minutes 29 seconds after that report.

Four minutes from "installed" to "it crashes"

TimeWhat happened
22:47A commit adds the tutorial and switches haptics to VibrationEffect composition primitives
22:58Agent reports the S24 install as "no crash". The S24 then drops off adb, so no screenshot. Asked "So is it tested?", it says the S24 was only installed and launched, and the S21 had "automated tests complete"
23:02Operator: it errors out in the tutorial. On the S21, with progress cleared, monkey seed 7 crashes the app at event 15 of 800
23:07Fix committed; the fresh-install monkey script follows 15 seconds later

The agent's mistake was in what "no crash" rested on: am start -W returning Status: ok and a 857 ms launch time. Nothing on screen was ever tapped. (The logcat it read did contain a FATAL EXCEPTION, from a Samsung system app on September 30. The agent correctly ignored it.)

Cause: Vibrator.vibrate without the VIBRATE permission

Ten minutes before the install, a commit replaced View.performHapticFeedback with Vibrator.vibrate(VibrationEffect.startComposition()…). The code comment gives the reason: on Samsung devices CONTEXT_CLICK is barely felt.

The two APIs have different rules. View haptics need no permission. Vibrator.vibrate needs android.permission.VIBRATE, and the manifest did not declare it. The game buzzes every time an arrow leaves the board, so the very first tutorial tap was the crash.

E AndroidRuntime: FATAL EXCEPTION: main
E AndroidRuntime: Process: (pre-release package name), PID: 12034
E AndroidRuntime: java.lang.SecurityException: vibrate: Neither user 10322 nor current process has android.permission.VIBRATE.

The fix touched two files, six lines added and one removed: declare the permission, and fall back to view haptics if the vibrator call fails for any reason.

<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.VIBRATE" />
runCatching { v.vibrate(VibrationEffect.startComposition().addPrimitive(primitive, scale).compose()) }
    .onFailure { view.performHapticFeedback(fallback) }

VIBRATE is a normal permission, granted at install with no dialog. Leave it out and the debug build still compiles.

Why the scripted tests missed it

Two device scripts were running on the S21 at the time. The tutorial script taps the three tutorial lessons in a fixed order. The level script writes a progress file to jump to a given level, then solves the board. Neither had a real pass condition. The tutorial script stops only if it cannot find the "Next" button, and the level script prints how many taps it sent. Neither looked for a crash in logcat or checked that the process was still alive.

The agent's own explanation was that the scripts only tap a fixed path. That is half right. The bigger hole was a check that never looked at crashes. (The tutorial script did run to the end on the S21 at about 22:45. Whether that build already had the vibration change was not checked that night, and the log does not say.)

The level script also writes tutorialDone=true when it jumps to a level, so it skips the first screens a new player sees by design. The new-player path only exists when the app has no data.

Running into the same problem? Email us what you are seeing and we will reply. Email us

The fresh-install monkey script

The monkey script loops over three fixed seeds (7, 21, 99). For each one it wipes the app's data, launches it, sends 800 random events, and counts FATAL EXCEPTION lines in logcat. Any non-zero count fails the run. Below is the core of the current version, without device selection, output cleanup and the exit code. The script defaults to the debug package; here it uses the release package published on Play.

PKG=com.sugarmount.arrows
adb shell setprop debug.firebase.analytics.app $PKG
for seed in 7 21 99; do
  adb shell am force-stop $PKG
  adb shell pm clear $PKG
  adb logcat -c
  adb shell am start -W -n $PKG/sugar.arrows.MainActivity
  sleep 2
  adb shell monkey -p $PKG --pct-touch 90 --pct-motion 10 --pct-nav 0 --pct-majornav 0 \
    --pct-syskeys 0 --pct-appswitch 0 --throttle 120 -s $seed 800
  n=$(adb logcat -d | grep -c "FATAL EXCEPTION")
  echo "seed=$seed fatal=$n"
done
  • -p keeps events inside this package.
  • --pct-touch 90 --pct-motion 10: 90% taps, 10% drags. Navigation, system keys and app switching are set to 0 so the run stays in the game.
  • --throttle 120 waits 120 ms between events. The last argument, 800, is the event count, so a run takes at least 96 seconds.
  • -s fixes the seed, which replays the same event sequence. Before the fix, seed 7 printed System appears to have crashed at event 15 of 800 using seed 7. After it, the same seed injected all 800.

"Fresh install" here means no app data at all. The first version deleted a single progress file through run-as, which only works on debuggable builds. When release signing went in on October 3, it became pm clear, with the comment "works on release (non-debuggable) builds too". If you suspect the install itself, run adb uninstall and install again. The script does not reinstall per seed; it clears data.

The pass condition changed too. The first version counted every FATAL EXCEPTION on the device, which also counts other apps' crashes, like the Samsung one on the S24. On October 4 the block puzzle game's script began counting only Process: <package>, lines plus am_anr entries from the events buffer. Its comment notes that uiautomator and the monkey tool can die on their own. On October 18 both scripts gained a setprop debug.firebase.analytics.app call before the loop. That makes test runs visible in Firebase DebugView, but it does not keep them out of the GA4 reports; that takes a separate developer traffic data filter on the GA4 property (corrected 2026-10-26).

(During the post-fix check, the S21 briefly disconnected in the middle of seed 21. Any run that printed - waiting for device - was thrown out and repeated.)

The rule: no "done" without a fresh-install monkey run

After that night the agent's memory gained one rule. Before calling an Android build tested, run the fresh-install monkey script on the connected device, on top of the fixed-path scripts, and name every device it ran on. Always run it when the manifest, a permission or a system-service call changes. The rule also includes the line "installing is not verifying".

Commit messages changed after that. As of October 19, 2026, 19 of the 144 commits made after the monkey script went in mention monkey in the message, and 16 of those report a result, in lines like "release (R8, test ads) monkey 3x1500 0 fatals" and "Android 7 launch and monkey pass on API 24". The other three are a tool list or a "still to run". Reported event counts range from 600 to 4,000.

When an agent says "done", ask which device and what ran on it. Without a monkey result from clean app data, we do not accept it as done. The wider pre-release routine is in What to check before shipping an AI-built Android app, and how we pin rules like this one for the agent is in How to write AGENTS.md for an AI coding agent.

The next day (October 2) a new stress suite crashed the game 28 times on its first pass through 300 levels: a blocked arrow springing back from far away overshot and read points[-1], an IndexOutOfBoundsException that got its own fix. A fresh-install monkey run starts at the tutorial and the first level, so deep levels need their own runs.

If you want to try this on your own app

  • Start from cleared app data (pm clear). A script that writes progress first skips the screens a new player sees.
  • Fix the seed, so you can replay the failing event sequence and confirm the fix with the same seed.
  • Make the pass condition a number: zero FATAL EXCEPTION lines and zero ANRs for your own package.
  • Always run it when the manifest, a permission or a system-service call changes. This crash came from exactly that kind of change.

What is still open

Arrow Knots' monkey script still counts every FATAL EXCEPTION on the device and ignores ANRs. It should match the block game's script and count only its own process's crashes plus ANRs. Several agent sessions share the same phones, so another app's crash failing our run is the first thing to fix.

Questions or ideas?

Send us where you got stuck applying this, a question about the numbers, or a topic you would like covered.

Email us sugarmount21@gmail.com

When green does not mean tested: all 6 parts

  1. AI agent says all tests pass: 7 E2E runners with zero expect()

FAQ

Do I need to ask the user for the VIBRATE permission?

No. VIBRATE is a normal permission, granted at install once it is declared in AndroidManifest.xml. View.performHapticFeedback works without it, but calling Vibrator.vibrate without the declaration throws a SecurityException and kills the app.

How many seeds and events should an adb monkey run use?

Our default is three seeds (7, 21, 99) at 800 events each, and five commits record release builds with test ads run at 1,500 events per seed. Fixing the seed is what lets you replay the exact sequence that failed.

Can I run monkey on a build with live ads?

We never do. Random taps on real ads are invalid clicks and put the AdMob account at risk, so monkey and other automated taps only run on builds using Google's test ad IDs.

If unit tests pass, can I skip the monkey run?

Not if you want to catch this kind of crash. All 31 engine unit tests passed that night. Permission checks happen in the device's system service, so a JVM unit test never sees them.

Sources: the game's git history and the agent's session log from that night (Korea time; checked October 19, 2026).

This note is written from values SugarMount measured itself; an AI coding agent was used to draft it.

item.title: Building an Android HWP viewer with rhwp: measured – SugarMount
item.description:
AX notes · Measurement

Building an Android HWP viewer: rhwp in a WebView, measured on 222 documents

Running the open-source rhwp engine inside an Android WebView, 221 of 222 Korean HWP and HWPX files opened on a Galaxy S21, with a median of 1.2 to 1.5 seconds from tap to first page.

Building the SugarDoc HWP viewer 2/8

To show Korean HWP documents in an Android app, you first need an engine that can draw them. Before writing HWP Viewer SugarDoc, we wanted to know whether the open-source rhwp engine could carry an app at all, so on October 3, 2026 we opened 222 files one by one from a cold start on a Galaxy S21 (Android 15). 221 opened. The engine passed, with two catches. Drawing every page of a 384-page file pushed the WebView renderer to 2.8 GB, and the set the first report called "24 government documents" held only 17 real government attachments.

HWP, HWPX and why a viewer is hard

HWP is the file format of Hancom Office Hangul, the word processor that Korean government offices, schools and many employers still use. HWP 5 is a binary compound file; HWPX is the newer ZIP-and-XML version; very old files are HWP 3.0. On a phone they usually arrive as attachments in KakaoTalk (Korea's main messenger) or email.

Layout is the hard part. Government press releases lean on dense tables, logos and fixed line breaks, and exam papers add equations and two-column pages.

Setup: one phone, 222 files, a cold start each time

rhwp is an open-source HWP/HWPX parser written in Rust and compiled to WebAssembly. It renders each page as SVG and is MIT-licensed. We used the npm package @rhwp/core 0.8.6, and the shipped app is still pinned to that version.

The test app was a single WebView with rhwp and the font stylesheet rhwp ships (153 font rules). For every file the app was force-stopped and relaunched; the first three pages went into the DOM and the rest were only timed.

  • Attachments from Korea's government policy portal, korea.kr: 17 files downloaded on 2026-10-02 (14 press releases; 13 HWPX, 4 HWP).
  • 198 samples from the rhwp repository, each with a reference PDF printed from Hancom Office 2020 or 2022, so page counts and first-page images can be compared. Many are hard cases: exam papers, equations, converted HWP 3.0 files.
  • Seven more files, explained in the section on what the AI got wrong.

We had no low-end phone.

Results: 221 of 222 opened

"Tap to first page" is app launch time plus first-page render time, so it includes the cold start. p90 is the value where the slowest 10% begin. Renderer memory is the PSS (proportional set size: private memory plus a fair share of shared pages) of the WebView renderer process.

Metrickorea.kr, 17 filesFirst report's "24 government documents"rhwp samples, 198
Opened17/1724/24197/198
Tap to first page, median1.4 s1.5 s1.2 s
Tap to first page, p901.6 s2.1 s1.9 s
Tap to first page, max1.8 s3.0 s3.3 s
Render per page, median-10 ms6 ms
Renderer memory (PSS), max286 MB391 MB422 MB

The one failure is a stress-test file from the rhwp repository, built around a giant table split across pages; it ran past the 120-second limit. The spike report made a fallback path a condition for adopting the engine, and the app now lets you keep waiting or hand the file to another app after 10 seconds.

Fidelity held up. Against the reference PDFs, page counts matched for 195 of 197 samples (the other two were one page off), and the median first-page image similarity was 0.997. We also put seven files (two press releases, five samples) side by side with Hancom's output. The press-release tables, logos and bold text and the exam paper's equations and two columns looked nearly the same. The one visible miss was the first question number, "문1)", dropped from one exam paper.

Running into the same problem? Email us what you are seeing and we will reply. Email us

A 384-page file only works if you draw the visible pages

One rhwp sample is a 384-page government administration handbook (10.7 MB). With every page's SVG in the DOM, the WebView renderer process grew to 2.8 GB. Drawing only the visible pages, the same file sat at 255 MB in one run and 366 MB in another run the same afternoon.

If you build an HWP viewer on a WebView, put virtual scrolling (only the visible pages and their neighbours in the DOM) in from day one.

The shipped viewer gives every page an empty slot of the right size and keeps SVG only for the visible pages plus two on each side, or one on each side on low-memory devices. Rendered SVG strings live in a byte-capped LRU (least recently used) cache, so the pages viewed longest ago are dropped first.

Fonts went from 144 MB to 9.2 MB

The font folder that comes with rhwp is 87 files and 144,327,972 bytes. The spike report called it "138 MB", which is the same number counted in mebibytes. The 222 documents actually used 17 of those files, about 37 MB.

The app ships 10 files, 9,207,952 bytes, about 6% of the original. Two rules decided what went in: a clear license and a close look. Hancom's own Hamchorom fonts were left out because Hancom's license page does not spell out whether they may be bundled in an app; Hamchorom Batang is drawn with Noto Serif KR and Hamchorom Dotum with NanumGothic, both under the SIL Open Font License. rhwp's NanumGothic was a subset that kept the reserved font name, so we swapped in the original TTF from google/fonts.

On 2026-10-05 we measured the cost on the same S21: how much first-page ink overlap (F1) against the reference drops with the substitute fonts. The pass mark, fixed in advance, was a median drop of 0.02 or less; the median came out at 0.0071. One file went over at 0.0336, a college entrance exam (Suneung) paper whose title is in Chinese characters (hanja). The difference sat in the hanja title and the circled numbers ① to ⑤, which the bundled fonts lack, so the system font draws them.

What the AI got wrong, and what verification changed

An AI coding agent (Claude) session ran the engine spike and wrote its report. Two days later, the follow-up experiments split the work: one agent measured, a separate verifier agent reopened the evidence files and recomputed every number, and only corrected values went into the docs. The first report's statistics were recounted at that point.

First reportAfter verification
24 real government documents17 korea.kr files (14 press releases) plus 7 others: 4 byte-identical to samples, 3 rhwp test fixtures
Samples: 177 HWP, 21 HWPX180 HWP, 18 HWPX (9 of them HWP 3.0)
Number recall around 0.9A bug in the comparison script: text runs were joined with no separator, so 11:00 and 10. 2. became 11:0010. 2.. Fixed, all 17 korea.kr files score 1.0 (a lenient upper bound)
Bundled fonts 9,700 KB (the follow-up's measuring agent)KiB written as KB; 9,933,636 bytes is 9.93 MB (later cut to 9,207,952 bytes)

"24 of 24 government documents" reads well, and 7 of the 24 were not government documents. Counted alone, the 17 real files were faster (1.4 s median) and lighter (286 MB max). The engine decision did not change, but without the verifier we would have published a number with the wrong provenance.

Writing this note, we recomputed the medians once more from the raw result JSON. The report's 1.5, 2.1 and 3.0 seconds came out exactly; the 366 MB run of the 384-page file turned up then. (The verification report also flagged that another script had overwritten one raw file, which must be regenerated before anyone quotes it.)

If you are testing a document engine

  1. Count the files your users really receive (government attachments, say) apart from the engine's own samples. Mixing them gives numbers with the wrong provenance.
  2. Force-stop the app before every file and time tap to first page. Record p90 and the maximum, not just the median.
  3. Measure renderer memory on your longest file. With hundreds of pages, build virtual scrolling in from the start.
  4. Bundle only fonts the documents actually use and whose licenses you have checked, and set a pass mark for how much the substitutes may change the layout before you measure it.
  5. Give files that hit the time limit a way out: keep waiting, or open in another app.
  6. Have a second agent or a person recompute the report's numbers from the raw data.

Still open

  • Low-end phones. According to the development plan, the Firebase Test Lab low-end run has not happened yet, so we do not know how a 400 MB renderer behaves on a 3 to 4 GB phone.
  • Hanja-heavy documents. The 0.0336 is only recorded, from a sample of two.
  • Upgrading rhwp. It is pre-1.0, so the app pins 0.8.6 and every build checks that the engine files match the pinned copy. An upgrade will be re-measured on the same 222 files. The other pre-release checks are in What to check before shipping an AI-built Android app.

Questions or ideas?

Send us where you got stuck applying this, a question about the numbers, or a topic you would like covered.

Email us sugarmount21@gmail.com

Building the SugarDoc HWP viewer: all 8 parts

  1. Three agent designs, three judges: the market judge alone would have picked the one that crashed on every KakaoTalk file
  2. On Android, HWPX can arrive as application/octet-stream: an 18-row intent matrix and the intent filter that fits it

FAQ

Can rhwp be used in a commercial Android app?

Yes. rhwp is MIT-licensed, but the Rust crates compiled into its WASM (Apache-2.0, BSD and others) need their notices too. The fonts it ships carry their own licenses and need checking file by file. HWP Viewer SugarDoc bundles 10 font files with confirmed licenses, OFL and others, and leaves out Hamchorom.

Why does a WebView HWP viewer use so much memory?

Every rendered page stays in the DOM as SVG. A 384-page file took the renderer to 2.8 GB with all pages drawn and 255 MB with only the visible ones.

Does one engine open both HWP and HWPX?

Yes. rhwp 0.8.6 opens both, and 221 of the 222 mixed files here opened. The difference between the two formats is explained in HWP vs HWPX: what differs and how to open both. If an HWPX file from a chat app will not open on your phone, see How to open an HWPX or HWP file on Android.

Sources: the engine spike report in the SugarDoc repository (measured 2026-10-03), the follow-up verification report (10-05) and a recount from raw data (as of 10-19).

This note is written from values SugarMount measured itself; an AI coding agent was used to draft it.

More AX notes

  • Verifying an AI agent's "done" report: 95.2% vs a 92.3% cap
  • 4.5:1 contrast in the site build: the dark hover pair that failed for 7 of 11 apps

item.title: About SugarMount: independent Android apps
item.description:
About SugarMount

SugarMount is an Android app brand run by simpest, an independent developer, making small apps that each do one job. Ten of them are on Google Play, from a Korean spelling checker and an HWP viewer to photo tools and two puzzle games.

Who makes the apps

SugarMount is the developer name used by simpest, an independent developer, to publish apps on Google Play. Planning, development, releases and support are all done by the same person. It is not a company or a team.

The author, Stephen

The AX notes are written under the pen name Stephen, the same solo developer who makes the SugarMount apps. They record what happened while building, checking and running apps with AI agents such as Claude Code. Every number in a note was measured on our own runs and comes with its source and date.

The apps

As of October 18, 2026, ten apps are public on Google Play. Features, data handling and help articles are on the SugarMount apps list and each app's page.

Photo and video

  • Compress Image
  • Flip & Rotate Image
  • Convert Image JPG PNG WEBP
  • SugarAlbum

Documents and text

  • HWP Viewer SugarDoc
  • SugarSpeller
  • SugarClip

Everyday

  • SugarCard

Games

  • Arrow Knots
  • Block Turn

How the apps are built and checked

  • Built with an AI coding agent. The three photo apps, HWP Viewer SugarDoc and the two games were built with Anthropic's Claude Code. In their repositories, 195 of 212 commits (92%) carry an AI co-author line (git history, October 18, 2026). SugarSpeller has been updated the same way since August 2025. The agent writes code, tests and release scripts; a person decides ad placement, pricing and releases, and checks on real devices.
  • Release builds run on a device before upload. The three photo apps and HWP Viewer SugarDoc go through a release gate (leftover test ad IDs, empty config, policy URLs), two launches of the shrunk release build, and end-to-end tests on a real device. Details are in the release check note.
  • Policies come from the code. Privacy policies are written after checking each app's source code and SDK settings, and say nothing the code doesn't back.
  • Numbers carry a source and a date. Numbers on this site come from the app repositories' git history, changelogs and device QA reports, with the date they were taken. What we could not verify, we leave out.

The process and the measured numbers are written up in the AX notes.

Principles

  • Photos and documents stay on the device

    The apps that handle photos, videos and documents (Compress Image, Flip & Rotate Image, Convert Image, SugarAlbum, HWP Viewer SugarDoc) process files on the device without uploading them, and never modify or delete the originals.

  • No sign-up

    None of the ten public apps has a sign-up or log-in screen. SugarSpeller creates an anonymous ID, not linked to any name or email, to count daily use of AI explanations.

  • Policies that match the code

    Each app's privacy policy is written from its actual code, including what the ad and analytics SDKs send.

Privacy

What leaves the device differs by app. For example, SugarSpeller sends the text you check to the Naver or Daum (Kakao) spelling checker, while the photo apps send no photos. Each app's details are in the privacy policy list.

Contact

Questions and bug reports go by email. Including the app name, device model and Android version helps us check faster.

Email: sugarmount21@gmail.com (write an email)

Google Play: sugarmount developer page

item.title: Convert an HWP or HWPX file to PDF on Android – SugarMount
item.description:
Help · Android

Convert an HWP or HWPX file to PDF on Android

Open the HWP or HWPX file in HWP Viewer SugarDoc, tap ⋮ (More options) and then Save as PDF, and pick a folder. The PDF is made on your phone without uploading the document. Long documents are cut to the first 15 pages.

This guide is based on HWP Viewer SugarDoc 1.2.0, an Android app made by SugarMount. The Save as PDF menu item arrived in 1.2.0; on older versions use the print screen instead (see below). The screenshots show the app in Korean.

Without an app, and the catch

HWP and HWPX are Korean word-processor formats, and Android phones usually have no app that opens them. If the phone cannot open the file, it cannot print it to PDF either, so the app-free options are all off the phone:

  • Ask the sender for a PDF. They export it from the program that made it, so the layout matches best. You have to wait for a reply.
  • Save as PDF in a desktop HWP program. Good for long documents where layout matters. Needs a computer with the program.
  • Upload to a web converter. Nothing to install, but the file goes to that site's server. Avoid it for letters or forms with names, phone numbers or addresses.

Save as PDF in HWP Viewer SugarDoc

  1. Open the document — tap the HWP or HWPX file in KakaoTalk, email or your file manager and choose HWP Viewer from Open with or Share, or pick it with Find in my files inside the app.
  2. ⋮ → Save as PDF — tap ⋮ at the top right of the document and choose Save as PDF.
  3. Check the page notice — if the document is longer than the limit, the app tells you how many pages will be saved first. Tap Save to go on or Cancel to stop without making a file.
  4. Pick where to save — Android's save screen opens with the document's name plus .pdf filled in. Choose a folder and tap Save.
  5. Done — the message "Saved as a PDF." appears. The HWP or HWPX file you received is not changed.

Checked on a Galaxy S21 (Android 15) with the SugarDoc 1.2.0 release build on October 18, 2026: a 47-page HWP document showed the notice and produced a 15-page PDF, and a 3-page HWPX document was saved with all 3 pages.

Save through the print screen

Tap Print in the ⋮ menu to open Android's print screen (on versions before 1.2.0 the item is called Print or save as PDF). Under Select printer, choose the save-as-PDF option (its name varies by phone) to keep the result as a PDF file. Use this if Save as PDF fails; the same page limit applies.

"In Android 4.4 (API level 19) and higher, the framework provides services for printing images and documents directly from Android applications."

Source: Android Developers, Printing content

Which way to use

MethodPhone onlyUploadLengthUse it when
SugarDoc Save as PDFYesNoneFirst 15 pages (6 on low-memory phones)You need a short notice or letter as a PDF right now
SugarDoc Print → PDFYesNoneSame as aboveSave as PDF failed, or you are on a version before 1.2.0 (there the item is ‘Print or save as PDF’)
Ask the senderYes (you wait)NoneNo limitThe layout must match, or it is longer than 15 pages
Desktop HWP programNoNoneDepends on the programYou need to edit a long document first
Web converterYesTo their serverVaries by siteThe document has no personal information

Verdict: for a document of 15 pages or fewer that you need as a PDF now, Save as PDF in the app is the quickest. For longer documents or forms where layout matters, get a PDF from the sender or make it on a computer.

Limits and what to do when it fails

  • Only the first pages are saved. Usually the first 15, or the first 6 on phones with little memory. You cannot choose a page range.
  • Distribution-only documents cannot be saved. When printing and copying are locked, Save as PDF and Print do not appear in the menu.
  • PDF files have no Save as PDF. They are already PDFs, so only Print is offered, and a password-protected PDF cannot be printed.
  • Layout may differ slightly. If the original fonts are not on your phone, similar fonts are used, so line breaks and spacing can shift. Open the saved PDF and check it before you submit it anywhere.
  • If it will not open, it will not save. Documents locked by a company DRM program cannot be opened. If the file does not open at all, start with what to check when an HWPX file will not open.
  • No PDF-to-HWP. SugarDoc is a viewer only.

About the HWP format

HWP is the native format of the Hancom word processor widely used in Korea. Its specification is public, which is why other apps can read it. Hancom says (in Korean) that it published the HWP binary format and the HWPML markup language on June 29, 2010: "한컴은 2010년 6월 29일에 자사의 바이너리 포맷인 HWP와 마크업 언어인 HWPML을 공개하였습니다."

Source: Hancom download center, HWP and OWPML formats. For how .hwp and .hwpx differ, see HWP vs HWPX.

FAQ

Does saving as PDF cost anything?

No. Save as PDF and Print need no payment, and the app has no ads.

Is my document uploaded anywhere?

No. SugarDoc does not send documents to a server; the PDF is made on your phone. See the HWP Viewer SugarDoc privacy policy.

Where is the saved PDF?

In the folder you picked on the save screen. The folder shown first can differ by phone, so check its name before you tap Save. Afterwards you can find the PDF in your phone's Files app.

Can I convert a document longer than 15 pages in full?

Not in SugarDoc. Only the first 15 pages (6 on low-memory phones) are saved. For the whole document, ask the sender for a PDF or make it on a computer.

If I cancel on the save screen, is an empty file left behind?

No. Cancelling on the save screen creates no file.

Related guides

  • When an HWPX file will not open on your phone
  • HWP and HWPX: what is the difference

Get HWP Viewer SugarDoc

An Android app that opens Korean HWP and HWPX documents and PDFs straight from KakaoTalk or email, and reopens them on the page you were reading. No ads and no sign-up. Works on Android 10 and later.

Get HWP Viewer SugarDoc on Google PlayAbout HWP Viewer SugarDoc

This product was developed with reference to Hancom's public HWP document file (.hwp) specification. SugarDoc is not affiliated with or endorsed by Hancom Inc. Hancom and HWP are trademarks of Hancom Inc.

item.title: HWP vs HWPX: what differs and how to open both – SugarMount
item.description:
Help · Android

HWP vs HWPX: what differs and how to open both

HWP and HWPX are both Korean Hangul documents, but they are built differently, so renaming the file does not convert it. On an Android phone, open both with one viewer; converting HWPX to HWP needs the Hangul word processor on a PC.

This article uses SugarMount's Android app HWP Viewer SugarDoc (SugarDoc for short; shown as "HWP Viewer" on your phone). It cannot convert HWPX to HWP or HWP to HWPX. Editing (Pro) covers body and table cell text in HWP documents only; HWPX documents cannot be edited yet.

How HWP and HWPX differ

.hwp is the long-standing format of Hancom's Hangul word processor, common in Korean schools, offices and government. It is a binary compound file, so its contents are not human-readable. .hwpx is the newer open format (OWPML): the document is written as XML files packed into one ZIP archive.

Hancom states which versions support each format:

"HWP의 개방형 문서 형식인 OWPML은 HWP 2018 버전부터 ".owpml" 확장자로 지원하고 있으며, 하위 버전은 HWP 2010 버전부터 ".hwpx" 확장자로 지원하고 있습니다."

In English: OWPML, HWP's open document format, is supported with the ".owpml" extension from HWP 2018, and with the ".hwpx" extension from HWP 2010. The same page describes the .hwp 5.x format as the one used from HWP 2002 through HWP 2018. Source: Hancom Download Center, HWP/OWPML format (Korean, checked October 18, 2026).

So the same letter can arrive in either format. An app that reads only one of them cannot open the other, and changing the extension leaves the inside unchanged.

Side by side

Item.hwp.hwpx
Inside the fileBinary compound fileXML files in a ZIP (OWPML)
Hangul word processor support (per Hancom)5.x format from HWP 2002From HWP 2010
Rename the extensionDoes not work. The inside stays the same
Open in SugarDocYes, including old HWP 3.0Yes
Password-protectedOpens with the password. Password-protected HWP 3.0 files cannot be openedOpens with the password
Convert between them in SugarDocNo

Verdict: if you only need to read the document, the difference does not matter; one app that opens both is enough. The format only matters when you must send the file on to someone using a Hangul version older than HWP 2010. Then re-save it as .hwp on a PC, or send a PDF.

Without an app, and the limits

  • Renaming the file: does not work. A .hwpx renamed to .hwp is still a ZIP-based HWPX inside, so programs that cannot read HWPX still fail.
  • Re-saving in the Hangul word processor on a PC: the usual way to get .hwp. Open the file in a version that supports .hwpx, then save a copy and choose the .hwp file type. Menu names vary by version, and you need a PC with the program.
  • Asking the sender for another format: the most reliable. The author can re-save as .hwp or PDF with the fewest layout changes, but you have to wait for a reply.
  • Your phone's built-in apps: usually open neither. Android phones generally have a PDF viewer but no app for .hwp or .hwpx.

Open either format with SugarDoc

  1. Tap the file — In KakaoTalk, email or your file manager, tap the .hwp or .hwpx file and pick HWP Viewer from "Open with" or "Share". For a file already saved on the phone, use Find in my files in the app.
  2. Don't choose a format — There is nothing to pick. The app tells HWP, HWPX and PDF apart by reading the file's contents, not by the extension at the end of its name.
  3. Find it again later — Every document you open is listed with its format (HWP, HWPX or PDF). When the list grows, search by file name.
  4. Enter the password if asked — A password-protected HWP or HWPX file opens once you type its password. The password is not saved.

Screenshots are real app screens captured for SugarDoc's store listing. Menu names can differ slightly by app version and phone model.

What it cannot do

  • No format conversion. SugarDoc cannot turn HWPX into HWP or the other way round, and it cannot create documents. Editing (Pro) covers body and table cell text in HWP documents only.
  • You can keep a PDF. If the recipient has no Hangul word processor, or an old one, a PDF may be the easiest thing to send. See convert an HWP file to PDF on Android for the steps and page limits.
  • Layout may differ slightly. When the original font is not on your phone, a similar font is used, so line breaks and spacing can shift. Old HWP 3.0 files may differ more.
  • Some files will not open. DRM-protected documents, password-protected HWP 3.0 files and files over 1 GB cannot be opened. Distribution-only documents may not open, or show only a preview.
  • Other office formats are not supported. Excel, Word and PowerPoint files do not open.

If a file does not open at all, the cause is usually your phone's app settings rather than the format. Start with when an HWPX file won't open on your phone.

FAQ

If I rename .hwpx to .hwp, will it open?

No. Only the name changes; the file is still HWPX inside, so programs that cannot read HWPX still fail. To get a real .hwp, re-save it as .hwp in a Hangul word processor that supports .hwpx.

Can SugarDoc convert HWPX to HWP?

No. SugarDoc has no format conversion. It opens both formats, and you can keep the document as a PDF.

Which format should I ask for?

For reading, either is fine; an app that opens both shows them the same way. If you must forward the file to someone using a Hangul version older than HWP 2010, .hwp or PDF is safer.

Do very old HWP 3.0 files open?

Yes, SugarDoc opens them, though they may look more different from the original. Password-protected HWP 3.0 files cannot be opened.

Are my documents uploaded anywhere?

No. SugarDoc opens documents on your phone without uploading them, and it never changes the original file. See the privacy policy for details.

Related articles

  • When an HWPX file won't open on your phone
  • Convert an HWP or HWPX file to PDF on Android

Get SugarDoc

An Android app that opens Korean HWP and HWPX files and PDFs straight from the app you received them in, and reopens at the page you were reading. No ads, no sign-up. Android 10 or later. Contact: sugarmount21@gmail.com

Get SugarDoc on Google PlayAbout SugarDoc

This product was developed with reference to Hancom's public HWP file format documentation. SugarDoc is not affiliated with or endorsed by Hancom Inc. Hancom and HWP are trademarks of Hancom Inc.

item.title: How to open an HWPX or HWP file on Android – SugarMount
item.description:
Help · Android

How to open an HWPX or HWP file on Android

An HWPX or HWP file usually will not open on Android because the phone has no app for Korean word-processor documents. Install an HWP viewer, then choose it from Open with in KakaoTalk, email or your file manager.

This guide uses HWP Viewer SugarDoc, an Android app made by SugarMount; other HWP viewers work much the same way. Menu names vary a little by app version and phone. The screenshots are cropped from the app's Google Play screenshots of version 1.0.0.

Why the file will not open

  • No app can read it. Android phones usually come with something that opens PDFs, but nothing for .hwp or .hwpx. Tapping the file ends with a message that no app can open it.
  • The file arrives as an unknown type. Some apps hand over .hwpx as a generic file instead of a document, so a viewer you have installed may still be missing from the list of apps.
  • Another app is the default. If you once tapped Always for a different app, that app opens straight away without asking. If it cannot read HWPX you see a blank screen or an error.

HWPX is the newer of the two formats. Hancom, the maker of the Hangul word processor, says (in Korean) that its open format OWPML has been supported with the .hwpx extension since Hangul 2010:

"HWP의 개방형 문서 형식인 OWPML은 HWP 2018 버전부터 ".owpml" 확장자로 지원하고 있으며, 하위 버전은 HWP 2010 버전부터 ".hwpx" 확장자로 지원하고 있습니다."

Source: Hancom Download Center, HWP/OWPML format (Korean, checked October 18, 2026). The two formats are built differently; see HWP vs HWPX.

Without installing an app, and the catch

  • Ask the sender for a PDF. Every Android phone can show a PDF, and the layout matches the original best. You have to wait for a reply.
  • Open it on a computer with the Hangul word processor or another program that reads HWP. Not much help when you need the file on the go.
  • Upload it to a web viewer or converter. Nothing to install, but the document goes to that site's server. Avoid it for school letters, forms or anything with names, phone numbers or addresses.

When an HWP file from KakaoTalk will not open

  1. Install an HWP viewer — get an app that opens HWP and HWPX from Google Play. HWP Viewer SugarDoc shows no permission prompts after installing and needs no sign-up.
  2. Tap the file in the chat — tap the file in the KakaoTalk chat to download it.
  3. Open with another app — from the file screen's menu (⋮ or the share button) choose Open with another app, then pick HWP Viewer from the list. Tap Always if you do not want to choose every time.
  4. Go back when you are done — Back returns you to KakaoTalk. Documents you open collect under Received documents in the app, so you can find them later by file name without scrolling back through the chat.

The menu names and their place differ by KakaoTalk version and phone. The app's own home screen shows the same three steps under Open documents from KakaoTalk.

Files attached to an email

Tap the attachment in your mail app and a list of apps to open it with appears. Choose the HWP viewer there. If the mail app only downloads the file and shows no list, download it first and then use the steps in the next section. Each mail app shows attachments a little differently.

When the viewer is missing from the list

  1. Check the file-type setting — some apps send .hwpx without saying what kind of file it is. In HWP Viewer SugarDoc, Settings > Opening files > Show for all file types lets you pick the app even then. It is on by default; if you turned it off, turn it back on and tap the file again.
  2. Save the file to your phone — use Save or Download in the app you received it in. It usually goes to the Download folder.
  3. Pick it from inside the viewer — open HWP Viewer SugarDoc, tap Find in my files and choose the file. This uses Android's own file picker, so the app does not need access to all your storage.
  4. Or share it — if the app you received it in has Share, choose HWP Viewer from the share list.

When a different app opens instead

If another app opens with no list to choose from, that app is set as the default. Go to Android Settings > Apps > that app > Open by default (or a similar name on your phone) and clear its defaults, then tap the file again; the list of apps comes back. Android's developer guide describes how a default gets set:

"When there is more than one app that responds to your implicit intent, the user can select which app to use and make that app the default choice for the action."

Source: Android Developers, Intents and intent filters (checked October 18, 2026).

Which way to use

MethodPhone onlyUploadOpens HWPXUse it when
HWP viewer app (such as SugarDoc)YesNoneYesYou often receive HWP files on your phone
Ask the sender for a PDFYes (you wait)NoneNot neededIt is a one-off, or the layout must match exactly
Computer with an HWP programNoNoneDepends on the programYou need to edit the document
Web viewer or converterYesTo their serverDepends on the siteThe document has no personal information

Verdict: if HWP files reach your phone more than once in a while, install a viewer that opens both HWP and HWPX; the document stays on your phone. For a one-off file or a form you have to edit, ask for a PDF or use a computer.

If it still will not open

  • It takes a long time — if a document has not opened after 10 seconds, HWP Viewer SugarDoc lets you keep waiting or open it with another app. When the file has a built-in preview you can view that first.
  • It is password-protected — HWP, HWPX and PDF files with a password open once you enter it. Password-protected files in the old HWP 3.x format cannot be opened.
  • It is locked by a company security program (DRM) — such files open only in that company's own viewer. The quickest fix is to ask the sender for an unlocked copy or a PDF.
  • The download is incomplete or damaged — if the file size is zero or tiny, download it again. If the same file from someone else will not open either, the file itself may be damaged.
  • It looks different from the original — when the original fonts are not on your phone a similar font is used, so line breaks and spacing can shift. Check documents where layout matters on a computer.
  • You want to edit it — HWP Viewer SugarDoc Pro can change body and table cell text in HWP (Hangul 5.x) documents. It cannot edit HWPX documents yet or convert HWPX to HWP.

FAQ

Will renaming .hwpx to .hwp make it open?

No. The two formats are built differently, so changing the extension does not convert the file. Use an app that opens both.

Is my document uploaded anywhere?

No. HWP Viewer SugarDoc opens documents on your phone and does not send them to a server. See the HWP Viewer SugarDoc privacy policy.

Can I save the document as a PDF?

Yes. From version 1.2.0, tap ⋮ and then ‘Save as PDF’ to create a new PDF in a folder you choose; earlier versions save from the print screen. Long HWP documents are saved up to their first 15 pages. See converting an HWP file to PDF on Android.

Do I need to sign up or allow permissions?

No. There is no sign-up and no permission prompt after installing. Files reach the app through Open with, Share or Android's file picker.

Who do I contact if it still will not open?

Email sugarmount21@gmail.com with your phone model, Android version and the app you received the file in. You do not need to send the document itself.

Related guides

  • HWP vs HWPX: what differs and how to open both
  • Convert an HWP or HWPX file to PDF on Android
  • Developer note: on Android, HWPX can arrive as application/octet-stream

Get HWP Viewer SugarDoc

An Android app that opens Korean HWP and HWPX documents and PDFs straight from KakaoTalk or email, and reopens them on the page you were reading. No ads and no sign-up, and documents stay on your phone. With Pro you can change body and table cell text in HWP documents and save a new file. Works on Android 10 and later.

Get HWP Viewer SugarDoc on Google PlayAbout HWP Viewer SugarDoc

This product was developed with reference to Hancom's public HWP document file (.hwp) specification. HWP Viewer SugarDoc is not affiliated with or endorsed by Hancom Inc. Hancom and HWP are trademarks of Hancom Inc.

item.title: Resize an ID photo for Korean application uploads – SugarMount
item.description:
Help · Android

Resize an ID photo for Korean application uploads

Korean upload forms often cap ID photos at a file size such as 500 KB. You can fit your photo under that limit right on this page, crop it to 3.5 × 4.5 cm, or use the Compress Image app on Android.

The app steps use Compress Image 1.0.6, an Android app made by SugarMount. Rules differ by site, so we don't invent numbers here; the only example is the Korean passport photo, which has an official guide.

Shrink it right here

Pick a photo and a size limit, and this page makes a JPEG under it. 1 KB counts as 1000 bytes, the same as in the app.

Your photo is processed only in this browser and is never uploaded anywhere.

This tool appears when JavaScript is turned on in your browser.

You can also drag a photo onto this box. JPG, PNG and WebP work.

Size limit

Crop to an ID photo ratio

The crop is centred. If the face is off-centre, move the crop position. Photos are never enlarged.

Most browsers cannot read HEIC photos. Convert the photo to JPG first, then choose it again. Convert HEIC to JPG on a Samsung Galaxy phone shows how.

FileSizeWidth × height
Original
Result

Check the site's rules first

Photo fields on Korean application, job and government sites usually set three separate conditions. Meeting one of them is not always enough.

  • File size: written as "500KB 이하" (500 KB or less). This is what the app fits.
  • Pixel size: for example 413 × 531 pixels. A fixed ratio means the photo must be cropped to it.
  • File type: usually JPG (JPEG). The app always saves JPEG.

The rules are in the notice or next to the upload button. For any site not covered here, follow that notice.

Without an app, and the limits

  • Ask the photo studio for a file: studios can often hand over a digital file sized for submission. This is the surest route, but you need to go back if the photo is already taken.
  • Your gallery app's editor: most Android gallery apps can crop, which handles the ratio. Menu names and resize options vary by phone and version, so we don't list them. After saving, check the real file size and pixels in the photo's details.
  • For a passport photo, the government resize tool: the Ministry of Foreign Affairs passport site has an online passport photo resize tool (Korean only). You upload a photo, zoom and move it until the face fits a red dotted guide, then save. It accepts JPG or PNG under 1 MB, and the page says the result is not for ID, half-size or visa photos.

Shrink it with Compress Image

  1. Select photos: tap Select photos on the first screen and pick the ID photo. The app uses the Android photo picker, so it asks for no storage permission.
  2. Method: Fit to size: on the Options screen, choose Fit to size under Method.
  3. Pick the limit: under Size limit per photo, pick 100 KB, 200 KB, 500 KB or 1 MB, equal to or below the site's limit. If none matches, tap Custom and enter 20 to 20000 KB.
  4. Set the long edge if pixels are fixed: on the same screen, open Long edge, tap the custom option and enter 320 to 8000 px. The aspect ratio stays the same, so if you already cropped to the required ratio, the short edge follows. A photo cropped to 3.5 : 4.5 with a long edge of 531 comes out at 413 × 531 pixels.
  5. Check the result: tap Create results. Each photo shows its size before → after and its width × height in pixels. These are the real sizes of the files that will be saved.
  6. Save or share: Save all writes new files to Pictures/SugarCompress, and Share sends them straight to another app. Your original photos are not changed.

Screens are real app captures taken on an Android emulator in September 2026 for the Play listing, with sample pictures. Menu labels match the app's 1.0.6 source.

Korean passport photo upload rules

The passport site lists the files it accepts for online renewal (quoted in Korean, our translation below):

"파일 크기 500KB 이하, 파일 형식 JPG/JPEG"
"가로 413 픽셀(pixel), 세로 531 픽셀 사이즈 권장(가로 395~431 픽셀, 세로 507~550 픽셀 이내만 업로드 가능)"

File size 500 KB or less, JPG/JPEG. Recommended 413 pixels wide by 531 high; only 395–431 wide and 507–550 high can be uploaded. Source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs passport site, photo files for online applications, checked October 18, 2026. Rules can change, so check again before you submit.

The app can meet the size, the JPEG type and the long edge. It does not judge head size, the white background or whether the photo was taken in the last six months. The same page also advises against phone photos:

"휴대폰 등 모바일 기기로 촬영된 사진, 사진 편집 프로그램 등으로 과도한 보정을 한 사진은 여권 발급 시 사진이 실물과 다르게 표현될 수 있으므로 권장하지 않음"

Photos taken on phones or heavily retouched are not recommended, because they may look different from the person in the issued passport.

You can test the result with the site's online passport photo check. The site says this check is for reference and the real review may differ.

Methods compared

MethodSet a size limitCrop to a ratioSet pixelsWhere it works
The tool on this pageYes (20 KB–20 MB)Yes (3.5 × 4.5 and 3 × 4 cm, movable)Passport 413 × 531 onlyAny browser
Compress Image appYes (20 KB–20 MB)NoLong edge only (320–8000 px)Any site with a size limit
Gallery app editorVaries by phoneUsually (crop)Varies by phoneAnywhere on the phone
Passport photo resize toolNot statedYes (face to guide)Set by the toolPassport online application only
Studio fileIf you askYesIf you askWhen taking a new photo

Verdict: if the site only sets a file size, the app alone is enough. If it also fixes the ratio and pixels, as for passports, crop first (for passports, use the official tool), then use the app last for the size and long edge.

When it doesn't work, and limits

  • The app does not crop to a ratio. The aspect ratio stays as it is. Crop with the tool on this page, your gallery app or the passport tool first.
  • No enlarging. If the original is smaller than required, a larger long edge changes nothing. Get the original file or a studio file instead.
  • Pixels may shrink too. If lower quality still misses the limit, the app reduces the long edge and tries again, never below 320 px. Always check the pixel size on the result screen.
  • Misses are reported. "The size limit could not be reached. Try a larger limit." means no result file was made for that photo. Raise the limit or use a different photo.
  • Output is JPEG. Transparent parts of PNG and WebP become white. It won't help where PNG is required.
  • No dpi setting. If a site asks for a dpi value such as 300 dpi, check whether it also gives a pixel size to aim for.
  • No rule checking. Face size, background and when the photo was taken are up to you and the site's rules.

FAQ

The site counts 1 KB as 1024 bytes. Is that a problem?

No. The app counts 1 KB as 1000 bytes, so a file fitted to 500 KB is at most 500,000 bytes. That is below 500 KB counted in 1024-byte units (512,000 bytes), so it passes either way.

Does it change or delete my original photo?

No. Results are saved as new files in Pictures/SugarCompress, and the original stays as it was.

Is my photo uploaded anywhere?

No. Photos are processed on your phone and never uploaded. See the Compress Image privacy policy for details.

Does it work with HEIC photos from an iPhone?

Yes, if your phone can decode HEIC. The result is saved as JPEG. To change only the format, see Convert HEIC to JPG on a Samsung Galaxy phone.

Does it cost anything?

It is free with ads and handles 20 photos at a time. Pro, a one-time purchase, removes ads and handles 100 at a time. Each photo can be up to 50 MB and 50 megapixels.

Related articles

  • Compress a photo to under 100 KB on Android
  • Convert HEIC to JPG on a Samsung Galaxy phone
  • Unmirror a selfie on a Samsung Galaxy phone
  • PNG to JPG on Android with a white background
  • How the app does it (AX note): Fitting a JPEG under a file size limit: quality binary search, a predicted long edge, and a final check against the original

Get Compress Image

An Android app that shrinks photos for forms and uploads to under a size you set, such as 100 KB or 500 KB, and saves them as new files. Photos are processed on your phone and never uploaded; originals are kept.

Get Compress Image on Google PlayAbout Compress Image

item.title: Compress a photo to under 100 KB on Android – SugarMount
item.description:
Help · Android

Compress a photo to under 100 KB on Android

You can shrink one photo to a JPEG under 100 KB right on this page, with no upload. For several photos at once, an app that takes the limit in KB is easier.

This guide uses Compress Image (SugarCompress) 1.0.6, an Android app made by SugarMount. Gallery menu names vary by phone model and software version.

Shrink a photo to 100 KB right here

Pick one photo and this page makes a JPEG of 100 KB or less. You can choose another limit too. 1 KB counts as 1000 bytes, the same as in the app.

Your photo is processed only in this browser and is never uploaded anywhere.

This tool appears when JavaScript is turned on in your browser.

You can also drag a photo onto this box. JPG, PNG and WebP work.

Size limit

Most browsers cannot read HEIC photos. Convert the photo to JPG first, then choose it again. Convert HEIC to JPG on a Samsung Galaxy phone shows how.

FileSizeWidth × height
Original
Result

Without an app: Resize in the Galaxy Gallery

The built-in Gallery app on Galaxy phones can shrink a photo's dimensions. Samsung's support guide lists these steps:

  1. Open the photo in Gallery and tap Edit.
  2. Tap More options (the three dots) and choose Resize.
  3. Pick a percentage, tap Done, then Save. To keep the original, choose Save copy from More options before saving.

"Resizing the photo to be larger than its original size is not an option."

Source: Samsung UK, How to resize a photo in the Gallery app on your Galaxy phone. The same page notes: "The resize feature may not be supported depending on the model version."

Limits of this method

  • You choose a percentage, not a file size. You have to save, check the file size, and resize again if it is still too big.
  • A plain save can replace the original. Samsung's guide says that on Android 11 saving overwrites the original unless you pick Save copy.
  • One photo at a time. The guide covers editing a single photo.

Unlike the tool above, some image compression websites upload your photo to their server. For ID photos or document scans, that may matter to you.

Fit a photo under 100 KB with Compress Image

  1. Tap 100 KB — Under Quick start on the home screen, tap 100 KB. This sets the limit to 100 KB and opens the photo picker. You can also tap Select photos and set the limit on the next screen.
  2. Pick photos — Choose photos in the Android photo picker. The free version handles up to 20 at a time. Check the list and tap Next.
  3. Check the limit and create — On the Options screen, make sure the method is Fit to size and the size limit per photo is 100 KB. For another number, use Custom and enter 20 to 20000 KB. Tap Create results.
  4. Review the results — Each photo shows its original size and its new size. The new size is the real size of the file that will be saved. A photo that could not fit the limit is marked as failed.
  5. Save or share — Tap Save all to save new files in Pictures/SugarCompress. Originals stay untouched. Tap Share to send them right away.

These are real app screens taken for the Google Play listing (version 1.0.1), so the example uses a 500 KB limit. Button and menu names are the same in 1.0.6.

How the app fits a photo under 100 KB

Fit to size first adjusts JPEG quality between 95 and 40, looking for a high quality that still fits the limit. If even quality 40 is too big, it shrinks the photo's long edge step by step and tries again. It never goes below 320 px on the long edge and makes at most 20 attempts or 30 seconds per photo. If nothing fits, it says "The size limit could not be reached. Try a larger limit." and does not count that photo as a success.

Five sample photos at a 100 KB limit

On November 8, 2026 we ran five sample photos through a test build on an Android emulator (Pixel 8 Pro, API 35) with the limit set to 100 KB. Every original is 12 megapixels (4000 × 3000 or 3000 × 4000). All five came in under the limit, but the pixels left over differ a lot.

Sample photoOriginalResultResult pixels
Mountains2.63 MB95 KB3400 × 2550
Beach2.67 MB99 KB1918 × 1439
City at dusk3.28 MB95 KB1175 × 1567
Flower2.23 MB96 KB3400 × 2550
Document page3.63 MB97 KB1774 × 2365

The mountains and the flower kept a 3400 px long edge, while the city at dusk, full of tiny lit windows, dropped to 1567 px. If your form also asks for a pixel size, read the px value on the results screen before you upload. At 500 KB, as in the screenshot above, the mountains, beach and city photos kept all their original pixels.

The sample photos are computer-drawn test images, so real camera photos can come out differently.

To set the resolution yourself, choose 1280, 1920 or 2560 px, or a custom value from 320 to 8000 px, under Long edge on the Options screen. Photos are never enlarged.

500 KB, 200 KB and 50 KB work the same way

In the app, Quick start offers 100 KB, 200 KB, 500 KB and 1 MB. For any other number, use Custom on the Options screen, from 20 KB to 20000 KB. A low limit such as 50 KB makes the photo smaller and softer, and some photos may not fit at all. The limit applies to each photo separately; the app does not fit a group of photos into a total size.

Methods compared

MethodSet a KB limitPhoto uploadedOriginalSeveral photos
Gallery ResizeNo (percentage only)NoCan be overwritten; kept with Save copyOne at a time in the guide
Compression websiteDepends on the siteDepends on the siteKept on your phoneDepends on the site
The tool on this pageYes (20 to 20000 KB)No, processed in the browserKept; result downloads as a new fileOne at a time
Compress Image, Fit to sizeYes (20 to 20000 KB)No, processed on the deviceKept; results saved as new files20 free, 100 with Pro

Verdict: If a form sets a hard limit like "under 100 KB", the tool on this page is quickest for one photo, and an app that takes the limit in KB suits several. If you only want a lighter photo with no exact limit, the Gallery's Resize is enough.

When it fails, and what it can't do

These are the app's limits. The tool on this page handles one photo at a time, keeps recompressed results within 16 megapixels, and reports a failure if the long edge would have to go below 64 px.

  • A very low limit can fail. If the photo is still too big at the lowest quality and resolution, it is marked as failed. Raise the limit a little and try again.
  • Results are JPEG. Transparent areas in PNG or WebP become white, and animated images are not supported. If a form requires PNG, neither the app nor the tool on this page can help.
  • Photos are never enlarged. It can't raise a photo's resolution.
  • HEIC works only if your phone can decode it. Unsupported or unreadable files are skipped, and the app tells you how many.
  • Very large photos are refused. A photo over 50 MB or 50 megapixels is not processed.
  • No cropping to exact dimensions. For ID photos with set pixel sizes or ratios, see Resize a photo for Korean ID and application uploads.

FAQ

Is 1 KB 1000 bytes or 1024 bytes?

The app and the tool on this page count 1 KB as 1000 bytes, so a 100 KB limit means at most 100,000 bytes. If a site counts 1 KB as 1024 bytes, its 100 KB is 102,400 bytes, so a photo fitted this way is still under the limit.

What if my photo is already under 100 KB?

In the app, a JPEG result is never larger than the original. If the photo is already small enough, the app keeps it at original quality without recompressing and removes only location and camera info. The tool on this page hands back a JPEG that is already under the limit unchanged, so location and camera info stay in it.

Are my photos uploaded?

No. The tool on this page works only inside your browser. The app also processes photos on your phone, and neither photos nor file names are sent to a server. See the Compress Image privacy policy for details.

Does it cost anything?

The tool on this page is free. In the app, every method, including Fit to size, is free, and the free version shows ads. Pro is a one-time purchase that removes ads and handles up to 100 photos at a time. It is not a subscription.

Where are the saved photos?

The tool on this page saves to the folder your browser downloads to. The app saves new files in the Pictures/SugarCompress folder. You can also find them in your gallery app.

Related guides

  • Resize a photo for Korean ID and application uploads
  • Convert HEIC to JPG on a Samsung Galaxy phone
  • PNG to JPG on Android with a white background
  • Unmirror a selfie on a Samsung Galaxy phone

Get Compress Image

An Android app that shrinks photos for forms, uploads and messages to under a size you choose, such as 100 KB or 500 KB. Photos are processed on your phone and never uploaded, and originals stay untouched. Requires Android 10 or later.

Get Compress Image on Google PlayAbout Compress Image

item.title: Convert HEIC to JPG on a Samsung Galaxy phone – SugarMount
item.description:
Help · Android

Convert HEIC to JPG on a Samsung Galaxy phone

To turn HEIC photos you already took into JPG, use a converter app that saves new JPG files. Convert Image does several at once on your phone, without uploading, and leaves the originals untouched.

This article is based on Convert Image JPG PNG WEBP 1.0.3, an Android app made by SugarMount. If you want future photos saved as JPG from the start, read "Without an app" first.

HEIC vs JPG

HEIC is a file in the HEIF photo format, compressed with HEVC (H.265). JPG is far older, and almost every website, program and printer accepts it. That is why a HEIC photo that looks fine on your phone can be rejected by an upload form or fail to open on a PC.

Whether Android itself can read HEIC depends on the device. The supported formats table in the Android developer documentation says this about HEIF decoding:

"Android 9.0+ … Device optional. Check ImageDecoder.isMimeTypeSupported("image/heif") for 8-bit support. 10-bit decoding requires optional HEVC Main10 profile."

Source: Android Developers, Supported media formats

Without an app, and the limits

  • Turn off HEIF (high efficiency) saving in the camera — some phones have a camera setting for it. With it off, new photos are saved as JPG. The menu name and place vary by model and version. Photos you already took stay HEIC.
  • Conversion when sharing from the gallery — depending on the model, the gallery may have a setting that sends photos as JPG when you share them. It only applies to what you share, and may not leave a JPG file on the phone.
  • Convert on a PC — the PC program has to read HEIC, and you need to move the photos first.
  • Upload to a converter website — no install, but the photos go to that site's server. Avoid it for photos of faces, IDs or documents.

Convert HEIC to JPG with Convert Image

  1. Pick the photos — on the home screen tap Select photos or Pick from files and choose your HEIC photos. Use Pick from files to keep the original file names: the photo picker does not share names, so photos picked there are saved as "SugarConvert + time". The JPG for forms quick start (quality 90, transparent areas white) starts with JPG settings ready.
  2. Check the selection — the Selected photos screen shows the count and total size. If HEIC photos are included, a notice says they convert only where the device can decode them. Tap Next.
  3. Choose JPEG — under Output format on Convert options, choose JPEG and set the quality. The default is 90; lower values give smaller files. Then tap Create results.
  4. Check and save — the Results screen shows the real size and resolution before and after. Tap Save all. The JPG files are saved as new files in Pictures/SugarConvert; the original HEIC files are not changed.
  5. If some photos fail — a HEIC the device cannot decode is marked as failed on its own, and the rest continue. Retry failed only runs just those again. If they keep failing on the same phone, see "When it fails, and the limits".

Test record: during development, HEIC input was checked on a Galaxy S21 (Android 15) with version 1.0.1 (September 25, 2026). Results on other models depend on whether the device has a HEIC decoder.

Methods compared

MethodPhotos already takenUploadMany at onceUse it when
Camera HEIF setting offNot changedNoneNot applicableYou want future photos saved as JPG
Gallery share conversion (some models)Only when sharedNoneVaries by modelYou only need to send a few photos in a chat
PC programYesNoneDepends on the programThe photos are already on your PC
Converter websiteYesSent to a serverVaries by siteOnly for photos without faces or documents
Convert Image appYes, if the device can decode themNoneFree 20 per job, Pro 100You need JPG files on the phone to upload or attach

Verdict: to keep HEIC photos you already took as JPG files on your phone, a converter app is the quickest. If the problem is future photos, change the camera setting. Doing both means less converting later.

When it fails, and the limits

  • HEIC the device cannot decode is not converted. The app reads photos with the phone's own decoder. Without one, or for HEIC the device does not support (such as 10-bit), that photo fails. Use a PC instead.
  • EXIF data such as date taken and location is not copied. The new JPG has no photo metadata. The photo's orientation is applied when saving.
  • HEIF files holding several images are not supported. Image sequences such as burst shots are refused.
  • Size limits. Up to 50 MB and 50 megapixels per photo.
  • Quality does not improve. JPG compresses again, so even quality 100 is not better than the original. A file can end up larger than the original; the Results screen shows it when that happens.
  • The original HEIC stays. Results are new files, so you have both. Delete the originals in your gallery if you no longer need them.

FAQ

Where are the converted JPGs?

They are saved as new files in the Pictures/SugarConvert folder on your phone. You can also share them straight from the Results screen.

Are my photos uploaded?

No. Photos are converted on the phone only, and the app asks for no storage permission; it reads only the photos you pick. Anonymous usage statistics and error reports contain no photos or file names, and you can turn them off in Settings. Details are in the Convert Image JPG PNG WEBP privacy policy.

Is it free?

The free version converts up to 20 photos at a time. Pro is a one-time purchase that removes ads and allows 100 photos at a time. It is not a subscription.

Can I convert to PNG or WebP instead?

Yes. Choose PNG or WebP as the output format; you can even give single photos their own format. Saving as HEIC is not available.

Does converting HEIC to JPG lose quality?

JPG compresses again, so there can be a small difference. At the default quality of 90, most photos look the same as the original. Raise the quality if detail matters, lower it if file size matters.
